definition_zh: 膝部；一圈；一段路程；舔食；轻拍
definition_en: the flat area of the legs when sitting, one circuit of a track, a stage of a journey, or the act of drinking with the tongue
core_image: 老人坐在藤椅上，膝头摊开一本旧相册
scene: 傍晚，老人坐在门廊的藤椅上，翻着一本旧相册。The child fell asleep on her mother's lap before the story ended.
sceneCN: 这里是「膝部」（第 1 个义项：人坐着时大腿到膝盖的区域）；句意为故事还没讲完，孩子就在母亲的膝上睡着了。可辨识画面：门廊、藤椅、旧相册。

derivatives.zh: 由 lap 与 top 复合，本指放在膝上使用的电脑，义为「笔记本电脑」
由 lap 与 dog 复合，义为「养在膝上的宠物狗」
由 lap 加 -ful（满……的量）构成，义为「一膝之量」

senses.title: The flat area of the legs when sitting
senses.definition: the flat space formed by your thighs when you are sitting down
senses.definitionCN: 坐着时由大腿形成的平坦区域
senses.example: She held the baby on her lap.
senses.exampleCN: 她把婴儿抱在膝上。
senses.why: The word first named a fold of cloth hanging over the legs, and from that covered area it came to mean the legs themselves.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指垂在腿前的衣摆，从被衣摆盖住的这片区域转指腿本身。

senses.title: One circuit of a racing track
senses.definition: one complete circuit of a track, as in a race
senses.definitionCN: 跑道上完整的一圈，如比赛中的一圈
senses.example: He set the fastest lap of the race.
senses.exampleCN: 他跑出了这场比赛的最快一圈。
senses.why: A lap was once a fold or a length of something, and the sense of one length around a course grew from covering the same ground again.
senses.whyCN: lap 曾指一段折叠或长度，绕行全程一遍的意味就从「又走完一段同样的路」长出来。

senses.title: One stage of a journey
senses.definition: one stage of a longer journey or race
senses.definitionCN: 较长旅程或比赛中的一个阶段
senses.example: The last lap of the tour took them north.
senses.exampleCN: 旅程的最后一段把他们带向北方。
senses.why: If a lap is one measured stretch, a journey becomes a series of such stretches, so the word names each of them.
senses.whyCN: 既然一圈是量好的一段，旅程就成了若干段这样的叠加，这个词便逐段指称。

senses.title: To drink with the tongue
senses.definition: to drink by moving the tongue, as animals do
senses.definitionCN: 像动物那样用舌头舔着喝
senses.example: The cat lapped the milk from the bowl.
senses.exampleCN: 猫舔着碗里的牛奶。
senses.why: Old English had a separate verb lapian for licking up liquid, and it simply merged in spelling with the noun.
senses.whyCN: 古英语另有一个动词 lapian 表示舔饮液体，它只是在拼写上与名词合并了。

senses.title: To wash against a surface softly
senses.definition: to move against a surface with a soft, repeated sound
senses.definitionCN: 带着轻柔的重复声响拍打表面
senses.example: Small waves lapped the side of the boat.
senses.exampleCN: 细浪轻拍着船舷。
senses.why: Water touching a surface again and again imitates the licking motion, so the licking verb stretched to waves.
senses.whyCN: 水一遍遍触碰表面，像重复舔舐，于是「舔」的动词被拉去形容波浪。

intro.en: Two Old English nouns and one Old English verb lie behind this word, and racing later gave it the sense of a circuit.
intro.cn: 两个古英语名词与一个古英语动词构成了这个词，赛马后来又给了它「一圈」的意思。

items.en: Læppa meant a fold or flap of cloth, the piece that hangs down over the body.
items.cn: læppa 意为布料的褶、垂下的衣摆。

items.en: A separate verb lapian meant to lick up liquid with the tongue.
items.cn: 另有一个动词 lapian，意为用舌头舔饮液体。

items.en: Middle English lap moved from the cloth over the legs to the legs themselves.
items.cn: 中古英语的 lap 从盖在腿上的衣摆转指腿本身。

items.en: Racing and travel added the sense of one measured stretch of a course.
items.cn: 赛马与旅行加上了「赛道上一段、一圈」的意思。

items.en: Modern English keeps the noun for legs, circuits and stages, and the verb for licking and for waves.
items.cn: 现代英语保留名词的腿、圈与路段义，也保留动词的舔食与拍打义。

note.en: The look-alike group collects short words that differ by one letter; the near-meaning group collects words for knees, circuits and licking.
note.cn: 形近组收只差一个字母的短词；近义组收表示膝盖、圈与舔的词。

entries.definition: A small failure or a passing of time, from a Latin word for slipping.
entries.definitionCN: 小失误或时间的流逝，来自拉丁语中表示滑落的词。

entries.definition: To hit with the flat of the hand.
entries.definitionCN: 用手掌拍打。

entries.definition: To strike the hands together to make a sound.
entries.definitionCN: 双手相击发出声音。

entries.definition: To move up and down like a wing, or a flat cover.
entries.definitionCN: 像翅膀那样上下摆动；也可指扁平的盖片。

entries.definition: The joint in the middle of the leg.
entries.definitionCN: 腿中部的关节。

entries.definition: One complete trip around a course.
entries.definitionCN: 绕跑道完整的一趟。

entries.definition: To move the tongue over something.
entries.definitionCN: 用舌头划过某物。

entries.definition: One stage of a competition or process.
entries.definitionCN: 比赛或流程中的一个回合。

normalIntro.en: A fold of cloth, a lick of the tongue and a length around a track all ended up in one spelling.
normalIntro.cn: 一块衣摆、一舔舌尖与赛道一圈的长度，最终落进了同一个拼写。

normal.en: Lap began as a fold of cloth that hung over the legs, which is why the leg sense comes first.
normal.cn: lap 起于垂在腿前的衣摆，所以「膝部」义排在最前。

normal.en: Lapian was a separate Old English verb for licking, so the verb lap and the noun lap have different histories.
normal.cn: lapian 是另一个古英语动词，意为舔，所以动词 lap 与名词 lap 来源不同。

normal.en: On someone's lap is the fixed phrase for the sitting position, keeping the image of cloth over the thighs.
normal.cn: on someone's lap 是表示坐姿的固定搭配，保留了布盖在大腿上的画面。

normal.en: Lap up means to take in eagerly, like a cat licking up milk.
normal.cn: lap up 意为急切接受，像猫舔光牛奶。

normal.en: Laptop is lap plus top: a computer that sits on your lap.
normal.cn: laptop 是 lap 加 top：放在膝上的电脑。

abstract.en: A word for cloth became a word for legs, because what covers a thing can end up naming it.
abstract.cn: 一个指布的词变成了指腿的词，因为遮盖某物的东西最后可能代替它得名。

abstract.en: One spelling holds a fold, a circuit and a lick, three histories that met only in English.
abstract.cn: 同一个拼写装着衣摆、一圈和舔，三段历史只在英语里相遇。

abstract.en: A lap is a unit of return: you go all the way round and come back to where you began.
abstract.cn: 一圈是回归的单位：绕行全程，再回到起点。

examples.en: She held the baby on her lap.
examples.cn: 她把婴儿抱在膝上。

examples.en: He set the fastest lap of the race.
examples.cn: 他跑出了这场比赛的最快一圈。

examples.en: The cat lapped the milk from the bowl.
examples.cn: 猫舔着碗里的牛奶。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「赖」——赖在椅子上不肯起来，东西就搁在膝上；记住 lap 是膝部。

root: 名词来自古英语 læppa（衣摆），动词来自古英语 lapian（舔饮）；两者在现代拼写上合并。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the cloth-covered lap of a seated person; the senses then take one length around a course, one stage of a journey, and the licking motion of the tongue.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是坐着的人被衣物盖住的膝头；义项由此取「绕行一圈」「旅程的一段」以及舌头舔舐的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an open album resting on the knees of someone seated in a wicker chair.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本摊开的相册搁在藤椅上坐着的人的膝头。

branches.en: a child asleep across a mother's knees
branches.cn: 横躺在母亲膝上睡着的孩子

branches.en: a runner crossing the line to end a circuit
branches.cn: 冲过终点完成一圈的跑者

branches.en: a road sign marking the last stage of a tour
branches.cn: 标出旅程最后一段的路牌

branches.en: a cat's tongue touching the surface of milk
branches.cn: 猫舌碰到牛奶的表面

branches.en: small waves touching the hull again and again
branches.cn: 细浪一遍遍拍打船身

intro.en: Two Old English nouns and one Old English verb lie behind this word, and modern compounds keep the knee sense alive.
intro.cn: 两个古英语名词与一个古英语动词构成了这个词，现代复合词则让「膝」义延续。

latinIntro.en: Both the noun and the verb are Old English, with no recorded Latin cognate.
latinIntro.cn: 名词与动词都来自古英语，没有记录在案的拉丁同族词。

items.meaning: front of the legs when seated
lap plus top, a computer for the lap
items.meaningCN: lap 与 top 复合，放在膝上的电脑

items.meaning: a small dog kept on the lap
as much as fills a lap
full of, the amount that fills
to drink by licking, to accept eagerly

definition_zh: 主要地；大部分地；在很大程度上；（古）慷慨地
definition_en: mainly or for the most part, and to a great extent; an older sense of generously survives in literary use
core_image: 天平的一端压得很低，说明几乎所有重量都落在这一边
scene: 统计报告发布后，记者们围在发言人身边提问。The crowd was largely silent as the results were read out.
sceneCN: 这里 largely 指「大部分地、主要地」（第 1 个义项）；句意为结果被宣读时人群大体上保持沉默。图中可辨识物件：发布台、话筒、记者的笔记本。

pos.zh: 主要地；大部分地；在很大程度上

derivatives.zh: largely 的原级，源自拉丁语 largus，义为「大的；大量的」
由 large 加 -ness 构成，义为「巨大；宽广」
由 en- 加 large 构成，义为「扩大；放大」

senses.title: Mainly, for the most part
senses.definition: in the main, so that most of something is true or affected
senses.definitionCN: 总体上，指某事物的大部分为真或大部分受到影响
senses.example: The crowd was largely silent as the results were read out.
senses.exampleCN: 结果被宣读时，人群大体上保持沉默。
senses.why: The adverb grew from a word for abundance, so largely counts the greater part of a whole rather than measuring one point on a scale.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词来自表示「充裕」的词，所以 largely 数的是整体的较大部分，而不是在刻度上量某一点。

senses.title: To a great extent
senses.definition: to a high degree, so that something is greatly influenced or explained by a cause
senses.definitionCN: 达到很高的程度，指某事很大程度上受某原因影响或由它解释
senses.example: His early success was largely due to the people who taught him.
senses.exampleCN: 他早期的成功很大程度上归功于教过他的人。
senses.why: If most of a result comes from one source, that source acts to a great extent, which is how the proportion sense turns into a degree sense.
senses.whyCN: 如果一个结果大部分来自某一个来源，这个来源就起了很大的作用，于是「比例」义自然转成「程度」义。

senses.title: Generously, in abundance
senses.definition: in a generous or plentiful way, an older literary sense still found in older texts
senses.definitionCN: 以慷慨或丰足的方式，是旧时文学中仍可见到的较早义项
senses.example: The old lord gave largely to the poor of his village.
senses.exampleCN: 那位老领主对村里的穷人施舍很慷慨。
senses.why: Latin largus meant generous as well as abundant, and the earliest English adverb kept that open hand before the sense narrowed to mainly.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 largus 既指充裕也指慷慨，最早的英语副词保留了那只张开的手，后来词义才收窄为「主要地」。

intro.en: Largely is the adverb of large, whose Latin source meant generous and abundant before French gave it the sense of broad.
intro.cn: largely 是 large 的副词形式；large 的拉丁来源本指慷慨、充裕，后来法语才赋予它「宽广」的意思。

items.en: Largus meant abundant, generous and free in giving, with little idea of physical size at first.
items.cn: largus 意为充裕、慷慨、乐于给予，起初几乎不含物理大小的意思。

items.en: Old French large kept the Latin word and added the sense of wide or broad, so size entered the meaning.
items.cn: 古法语 large 承接拉丁词义，又加上「宽、阔」的意思，于是大小进入了词义。

items.en: Middle English large covered both generosity and breadth, and the adverb largely was built with -ly.
items.cn: 中古英语 large 同时含慷慨与宽广，副词 largely 由 -ly 构成。

items.en: Largely first meant in a generous or plentiful manner, then drifted towards for the greater part.
items.cn: largely 最初意为「慷慨地、大量地」，后来转向「大部分地」。

items.en: Modern English uses largely almost only for mainly or to a great extent, while the generous sense survives in literary or older use.
items.cn: 现代英语的 largely 几乎只表示「主要地、在很大程度上」，慷慨义只留在文学或较早用法中。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the large family and its adverbs; the near-meaning group collects other adverbs of proportion.
note.cn: 形近组收 large 一词族及其副词；近义组收其他表示比例的副词。

entries.definition: Big in size or amount, the adjective behind largely.
entries.definitionCN: 尺寸或数量大的，是 largely 背后的形容词。

entries.definition: To make something bigger.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物放大、扩大。

entries.definition: The quality of being large.
entries.definitionCN: 大的性质；巨大。

entries.definition: For the most part, more than anything else.
entries.definitionCN: 大部分地；首要地。

entries.definition: Usually or in most cases.
entries.definitionCN: 通常；大多数情况下。

entries.definition: Mainly, above all other things.
entries.definitionCN: 主要地，首要地。

entries.definition: Over a large area or among many people.
entries.definitionCN: 广泛地；在许多地方或许多人中。

normalIntro.en: The adverb counts the bigger part of a whole, and its Latin root still remembers generosity.
normalIntro.cn: 这个副词数的是整体中较大的那一部分，它的拉丁词根还记着「慷慨」。

normal.en: Large comes from Latin largus, which meant generous and plentiful before it meant big.
normal.cn: large 来自拉丁语 largus，在表示「大」之前，它先表示慷慨、丰足。

normal.en: Add -ly and you get an adverb that says most of the whole is on one side.
normal.cn: 加上 -ly 得到的副词，意思是整体的大部分都落在一边。

normal.en: Largely because marks the main cause, not the only cause.
normal.cn: largely because 标出主要原因，而不是唯一原因。

normal.en: Largely ignored means ignored by most people, while largely unchanged means changed only a little.
normal.cn: largely ignored 指被大多数人忽视；largely unchanged 指只改变了一点点。

normal.en: The generous sense survives in older writing, where giving largely means giving freely.
normal.cn: 慷慨义留在较早的文字里，giving largely 就是慷慨地给予。

abstract.en: A word for an open hand became a word for the bigger share: abundance turns into proportion.
abstract.cn: 一个形容张开的手的词变成了「较大份额」的词：充裕转成了比例。

abstract.en: To say largely is to leave a small door open, because most is not all.
abstract.cn: 说 largely 就是留一扇小门，因为「大部分」并不等于全部。

abstract.en: The adverb measures a crowd as one body, not as a hundred separate opinions.
abstract.cn: 这个副词把人群当成一个整体来衡量，而不是一百个各自独立的意见。

examples.en: The crowd was largely silent as the results were read out.
examples.cn: 结果被宣读时，人群大体上保持沉默。

examples.en: His early success was largely due to the people who taught him.
examples.cn: 他早期的成功很大程度上归功于教过他的人。

examples.en: The village is now largely deserted in winter.
examples.cn: 这个村子在冬天如今大都空着。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拉直了」——把大部分道理拉直说明白；谐音记住 largely 是主要地。

root: 由 large 加 -ly 构成；large 源自拉丁语 largus（充裕、慷慨），经古法语 large（宽、大）进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the greater part of a whole; the word then measures degree, and an older sense of generous giving survives at the edge.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是整体中的较大部分；词义由此转为衡量程度，而「慷慨给予」的旧义留在边缘。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balance with almost all the weight settled on one side.
core.cn: 核心意象：天平上几乎所有重量都压在一边。

branches.en: a mostly silent hall during an announcement
branches.cn: 宣布结果时大体安静的大厅

branches.en: a region that is mostly farmland
branches.cn: 大部分是农田的地区

branches.en: a success explained by one strong cause
branches.cn: 由一个强原因解释的成功

branches.en: a report left almost untouched
branches.cn: 几乎原封未动的报告

branches.en: an old lord giving freely to the poor
branches.cn: 老领主慷慨施舍穷人

intro.en: The word is an adjective plus the English adverb suffix -ly, and the adjective itself comes from a Latin word for plenty.
intro.cn: 这个词是形容词加英语副词后缀 -ly，而形容词本身来自一个表示「丰足」的拉丁词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 幼虫；昆虫自卵孵化后的幼期形态；毛虫、蛆、蛴螬等幼体；水生无脊椎动物的自由生活幼体；蝌蚪式的水生幼期；生命史中的幼体阶段；不成熟的雏形；面具与幽灵（拉丁语旧义）
definition_en: the immature feeding stage of an insect or other invertebrate, which later changes into the adult form; historically also a mask or ghost
core_image: 叶片背面趴着一条肉虫，身体一节一节，六只真足紧贴叶脉，身边是被啃出的缺口
scene: 叶片背面，一条幼虫紧贴叶脉啃出月牙形的缺口。A larva chews a crescent hole in the leaf while clinging to the vein.
sceneCN: 这里 larva 指「昆虫自卵孵化后的幼期取食形态」（第 1 个义项：幼虫）；句意为一条幼虫紧贴叶脉、在叶片上啃出月牙形缺口。可辨识物件：分节体躯、六只真足、叶脉、月牙形缺口。

pos.zh: 幼虫；幼体（昆虫或其它无脊椎动物）

derivatives.zh: 幼虫的；幼期的
larva 的复数
杀幼虫剂
产幼虫的（如某些蝇类）
幼虫形的

senses.title: The immature feeding stage of an insect
senses.titleCN: 昆虫自卵孵化后的取食幼期
senses.definition: the wingless, often worm-like stage that hatches from an egg and feeds before transforming
senses.definitionCN: 从卵中孵出、通常无翅且形似蠕虫、取食之后才转变的幼期
senses.example: A larva chews a crescent hole in the leaf while clinging to the vein.
senses.exampleCN: 一条幼虫紧贴叶脉，在叶片上啃出月牙形缺口。
senses.why: The word marks a stage, not a species: any insect that undergoes complete change passes through a larva before the pupa.
senses.whyCN: 这个词标的是阶段而非物种：任何完全变态的昆虫都要经过幼虫才到蛹。

senses.title: A caterpillar or grub
senses.titleCN: 毛虫、蛆、蛴螬等具体幼体
senses.definition: the familiar worm-like young of butterflies, beetles or flies, named by shape in everyday speech
senses.definitionCN: 蝴蝶、甲虫或蝇类的幼体，日常说法按形状称呼
senses.example: The caterpillar is the larva of a moth or butterfly.
senses.exampleCN: 毛虫是蛾或蝴蝶的幼虫。
senses.why: Everyday names such as grub, maggot and caterpillar split the general stage into recognizable shapes.
senses.whyCN: 蛴螬、蛆、毛虫这些日常名把笼统的幼期拆成可辨认的形状。

senses.title: The free-living young of water animals
senses.titleCN: 水生无脊椎动物的自由生活幼体
senses.definition: a swimming young stage of many marine invertebrates, such as the trochophore of a worm or the nauplius of a crustacean
senses.definitionCN: 许多海洋无脊椎动物的游泳幼期，如环节动物的担轮幼虫或甲壳类的无节幼虫
senses.example: The barnacle passes through a swimming larva before it settles.
senses.exampleCN: 藤壶在定居之前要经过一个游泳的幼体阶段。
senses.why: Zoology generalized the term from insects to any animal whose young differs sharply from the adult.
senses.whyCN: 动物学把这个词从昆虫扩大到任何幼体与成体差别很大的动物。

senses.title: The tadpole stage of amphibians
senses.titleCN: 两栖类的水生幼期（蝌蚪）
senses.definition: the aquatic, gilled young of a frog or salamander, which later metamorphoses into the adult
senses.definitionCN: 蛙或蝾螈具鳃的水生幼体，之后变态为成体
senses.example: The tadpole is the larva of a frog, and it breathes with gills.
senses.exampleCN: 蝌蚪是蛙的幼虫，用鳃呼吸。
senses.why: Amphibian biology borrowed the insect term because the same two-stage pattern appears, water young then land adult.
senses.whyCN: 两栖动物学借用了昆虫术语，因为出现了同样的两段式格局：水中幼体，陆生成体。

senses.title: A stage in a life cycle
senses.definition: the phase of a life cycle entered after hatching and left at metamorphosis, treated as a unit of timing
senses.definitionCN: 孵化之后进入、变态时结束的生命史阶段，被当作计时单位
senses.example: Larvae feed for weeks before the pupal stage begins.
senses.exampleCN: 幼虫取食数周之后才进入蛹期。
senses.why: This abstract sense measures development by stages; the noun becomes a slot in a schedule rather than an animal.
senses.whyCN: 这一抽象义用阶段来度量发育；名词成了时间表上的格子，而非动物。

senses.title: An undeveloped early form
senses.definition: anything that exists in an early, unformed state, compared to an insect that has not yet taken its adult shape
senses.definitionCN: 任何处于早期、尚未成形状态的事物，比作尚未长成成虫形态的昆虫
senses.example: The proposal is still a larva, all appetite and no structure.
senses.exampleCN: 这份提案还只是个幼虫，只有胃口，没有结构。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps the biological core: what is describes is feeding and growing, not yet finished.
senses.whyCN: 比喻保留了生物核心：所描述之物正在取食与生长，尚未完成。

senses.title: A mask or ghost
senses.definition: the original Latin sense of a mask, especially one worn by an actor, or a ghost haunting a house
senses.definitionCN: 拉丁语原义：面具，尤指演员所戴，或出没于屋中的幽灵
senses.example: In Latin, larva could mean a mask worn on the stage.
senses.exampleCN: 在拉丁语中，larva 可以指舞台上戴的面具。
senses.why: Linnaeus took an old word for mask and ghost and made it a scientific term, so the modern sense carries a trace of disguise.
senses.whyCN: 林奈把一个意为面具与幽灵的旧词变成科学术语，现代义因此带着伪装的痕迹。

senses.title: A juvenile form used as food or pest
senses.titleCN: 作为饵料或害虫的幼体
senses.definition: the young stage considered as a resource or a pest, as when larvae are sold as fish food or sprayed as crop pests
senses.definitionCN: 把幼期当作资源或害物，如作为鱼饲料出售或作为作物害虫喷杀
senses.example: Anglers buy larvae by the tub for bait.
senses.exampleCN: 钓鱼人按盒购买幼虫作饵。
senses.why: Economics and agriculture recast the stage as a product or a target, which is a further extension of the biological sense.
senses.whyCN: 经济与农业把这个阶段改读为产品或清除对象，是生物义的进一步延伸。

intro.en: Larva is Latin for 'mask, ghost'. Linnaeus adopted it in the eighteenth century for the young stage of an insect, and the entomological sense drove out the older one.
intro.cn: larva 在拉丁语中意为「面具、幽灵」。林奈在 18 世纪把它采用为昆虫幼期的名称，昆虫学义后来压过了旧义。

items.en: Latin larva meant a mask, especially a frightening one, and by extension a ghost or spectre.
items.cn: 拉丁 larva 指面具，尤指吓人的面具，并引申为幽灵、鬼魂。

items.en: Latin plural larvae came into English with the scientific term; the English plural larvas is rare and mainly historical.
items.cn: 拉丁复数 larvae 随科学术语进入英语；英语式复数 larvas 罕见，主要用于历史文献。

items.en: The step from 'mask' to 'caterpillar' is not fully explained; a common suggestion is that the young insect looks like a disguise of the adult, but this is a hypothesis.
items.cn: 从「面具」到「毛虫」的一步没有得到完整解释；常见说法是幼体看起来像成虫的伪装，但这只是假说。

items.en: Linnaeus fixed larva as the term for the immature stage in his eighteenth-century classification, and the word entered general English through natural history.
items.cn: 林奈在 18 世纪分类学中把 larva 定为幼期的术语，这个词经自然史著作进入一般英语。

items.en: Zoology later applied the term to the young of crustaceans, molluscs and amphibians, widening it well beyond insects.
items.cn: 动物学后来把这个词用于甲壳类、软体动物与两栖类的幼体，范围远超昆虫。

items.en: Source uncertain (detail and first date): the deeper origin and the exact first citation are not settled, so any pre-Latin form offered here is a reconstruction and competing hypotheses are left side by side.
items.cn: 来源不确定（细节与首见年代）：更深的来源与确切最早书证均无定论，此处给出的拉丁语之前形式属重构形式，并列假说一并保留、不作定论。

note.en: Group one holds words whose spelling or sound invites confusion with larva; group two holds biological terms for young animals.
note.cn: 第一组收拼写或读音易与 larva 混淆的词；第二组收表示幼体动物的生物学术语。

entries.definition: Lava comes from Italian and Latin labes 'a fall, a slide' and has nothing to do with insects; the two words differ by one letter.
entries.definitionCN: lava 来自意大利语与拉丁 labes「滑落」，与昆虫无关；两词只差一个字母。

entries.definition: Larval is the adjective built on larva, not a separate noun.
entries.definitionCN: larval 是由 larva 构成的形容词，不是另一个名词。

entries.definition: Larvae is simply the Latin plural of larva; using it as a singular is a common error.
entries.definitionCN: larvae 只是 larva 的拉丁复数；把它当单数用是常见错误。

entries.definition: This English-style plural appears in older texts but is not the standard form today.
entries.definitionCN: 这一英语式复数见于较早文献，今天并非标准形式。

entries.definition: A nymph is the young of an insect with incomplete metamorphosis; it already resembles the adult and has no pupal stage.
entries.definitionCN: nymph 指不完全变态昆虫的幼期；它已形似成虫，没有蛹期。

entries.definition: A grub is a thick, legless larva, typically of a beetle, and names one shape rather than the stage.
entries.definitionCN: grub 指粗壮无足的幼虫，多见于甲虫，是一个形状名称而非阶段名称。

entries.definition: Caterpillar names the larva of a butterfly or moth, usually with visible legs and a segmented body.
entries.definitionCN: caterpillar 指蝴蝶或蛾的幼虫，通常有明显足与分节的身体。

entries.definition: A maggot is the legless larva of a fly, found in decaying matter and used in medicine to clean wounds.
entries.definitionCN: maggot 是蝇类的无足幼虫，见于腐败物中，医学上也用于清创。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin larva first meant a mask or ghost; the insect sense is a later scientific borrowing.
normal.cn: 拉丁 larva 本指面具或幽灵；昆虫义是后来的科学借用。

normal.en: The family runs larva, larvae, larval, larvicide and larviparous.
normal.cn: 词族包括 larva、larvae、larval、larvicide 与 larviparous。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: larva stage, insect larva, larva migrans.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义项：幼虫期、昆虫幼虫、游走性幼虫。

normal.en: The standard plural is larvae, following Latin first-declension nouns.
normal.cn: 标准复数是 larvae，遵循拉丁第一变格法名词。

normal.en: Complete metamorphosis runs egg, larva, pupa, adult.
normal.cn: 完全变态依次为卵、幼虫、蛹、成虫。

abstract.en: Picture a mask left on a chair, still shaped like the face that wore it.
abstract.cn: 想象一张留在椅子上的面具，仍带着戴它那张脸的轮廓。

abstract.en: Picture a body that is all appetite and no wings.
abstract.cn: 想象一具只有胃口、没有翅膀的身体。

abstract.en: Picture a swimmer that will later glue itself to a rock and never move again.
abstract.cn: 想象一个游泳者，日后会把自己粘在岩石上，再也不动。

examples.en: Each larva moults several times before it is ready to pupate.
examples.cn: 每条幼虫在准备化蛹前要蜕皮数次。

examples.en: The larvae of mosquitoes breathe through a tube at the water surface.
examples.cn: 蚊的幼虫通过水面上的呼吸管呼吸。

examples.en: Fossil larvae show the feeding marks of ancient insects on leaves.
examples.cn: 化石幼虫在叶片上留下了远古昆虫的取食痕迹。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「larva（拉瓦）」——从卵里「拉」出来的小肉虫 → 幼虫

root: 拉丁 larva「面具、幽灵」；林奈 18 世纪采用为昆虫幼期术语。「面具」到「毛虫」的过渡未获完整解释，相关说法仅为假说。复数 larvae 为拉丁式，larvas 罕见。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses trace one stage: a worm-like feeder, its named shapes, its water-borne cousins, the amphibian version, the slot in a life cycle, the metaphor of immaturity, the old mask sense and the stage as product.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个阶段展开：蠕虫状的取食者、各种形状名称、水中同族、两栖版本、生命史中的一格、不成熟的比喻、旧时的面具义，以及作为产品的幼体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a segmented worm-like body with six true legs clamped to a leaf vein, eating a crescent hole.
core.cn: 核心意象：一具分节的蠕虫状身体，六只真足扣住叶脉，啃出月牙形缺口。

branches.en: THE FEEDER: the stage and its everyday shapes, caterpillar, grub and maggot.
branches.cn: 取食者：这一阶段及其日常形状——毛虫、蛴螬、蛆。

branches.en: OTHER WATERS: crustacean and amphibian young repeat the pattern outside insects.
branches.cn: 别处的水域：甲壳类与两栖类的幼体在昆虫之外重复同一格局。

branches.en: THE SLOT: life cycle timing turns the animal into a stage and a product.
branches.cn: 那一格：生命史的计时把动物变成阶段与产品。

branches.en: IMMATURE FORM: the metaphor keeps feeding and growing, without a finished shape.
branches.cn: 未成形：比喻保留取食与生长，尚无完成的形状。

branches.en: MASK AND GHOST: the Latin word for a disguise is the origin of the scientific term.
branches.cn: 面具与幽灵：意为伪装的那个拉丁词正是科学术语的来源。

intro.en: Larva is a Latin noun; English builds its family with Latin plurals and suffixes, and the larv- stem also appears in learned compounds.
intro.cn: larva 是拉丁名词；英语用拉丁复数与后缀构成词族，larv- 词干也出现在学术复合词中。

latinIntro.en: Latin larva, plural larvae, gives larval, larvicide and larviparous; the same stem appears in larvarium, a place for keeping larvae.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 larva（复数 larvae）衍生 larval、larvicide、larviparous；同一词干亦见于 larvarium，指饲养幼虫的场所。

items.example: Each larva feeds on one leaf.
items.exampleCN: 每条幼虫取食一片叶子。

items.example: The larvae hatch within three days.
The pond was treated with a larvicide.
Some flies are larviparous rather than egg-laying.
items.exampleCN: 有些蝇类直接产幼虫而非产卵。

items.example: The female beetle remains larviform as an adult.
items.exampleCN: 这种雌甲虫成年后仍保持幼虫形。

items.example: The lab keeps a larvarium beside the microscope.
items.exampleCN: 实验室在显微镜旁设了幼虫饲养箱。

items.example: Larva migrans produces a creeping skin line.
items.exampleCN: 游走性幼虫在皮肤上留下爬行线。

latinEntries.structure: larva, larvae (f., first declension, zoological use)
latinEntries.meaning: the young stage of an animal

definition_zh: 激光；激光束；激光器；激光技术
definition_en: a device that produces a narrow, intense beam of light; the beam itself; the technology that uses such beams
core_image: 一束极细的红色光线从仪器里射出，笔直穿过空气
scene: 手术室里，医生用一束极细的光切开组织，边缘几乎看不到血。The surgeon used a laser to remove the tissue without cutting.
sceneCN: 这里是「激光」（第 1 个义项：高度集中的光束）；句意是外科医生用激光去除组织，而不用刀切。图中可辨识物件：手术灯、仪器面板、红色光束。

pos.zh: 激光；激光束；激光器；激光技术

derivatives.zh: 由 laser 逆构而成的动词，义为「发出激光；用激光处理」
由激光角膜手术的英文首字母缩略而成，义为「激光视力矫正手术」
由 laser 与 guided 复合而成，义为「激光制导的」

senses.title: A narrow, intense beam of light
senses.definition: a narrow, very intense beam of light in which the waves travel together
senses.definitionCN: 波列高度一致、又细又强的光束
senses.example: The laser cut through the metal sheet in seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 激光几秒钟就切穿了金属板。
senses.why: The acronym was built to name light amplified into a tight, orderly beam, so the beam itself became the everyday sense.
senses.whyCN: 这个缩略词本是为描述被放大成紧密有序光束的光而造，于是光束本身成了日常义项。

senses.title: A device that produces such a beam
senses.definition: a machine or device that produces a laser beam
senses.definitionCN: 产生激光束的机器或装置
senses.example: The lab bought a new laser for the experiment.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室为这项实验买了一台新的激光器。
senses.why: Because the acronym first named the process and the apparatus, the device sense stayed beside the beam it produces.
senses.whyCN: 这个缩略词最初兼指过程和装置，所以「装置」义一直与它产生的光束并存。

senses.title: The technology or use of such beams
senses.definition: the use of laser beams in medicine, industry, scanning or entertainment
senses.definitionCN: 激光在医疗、工业、扫描或娱乐中的使用
senses.example: Laser is now common in eye surgery.
senses.exampleCN: 激光如今在白内障等眼科手术中很常见。
senses.why: As the device spread into hospitals, workshops and shops, the word came to stand for the whole technology rather than one beam.
senses.whyCN: 随着装置进入医院、车间和商店，这个词逐渐指整套技术，而不只是一束光。

intro.en: Laser is not an inherited word but a twentieth-century acronym, coined from the initials of a scientific phrase and then turned into an ordinary noun.
intro.cn: laser 不是世代相传的词，而是二十世纪由科学短语首字母造出的缩略词，随后变成普通名词。

items.en: Physicists were amplifying microwaves with a device called a maser and wanted the same effect with light.
items.cn: 二十世纪五十年代，物理学家用称为 maser 的装置放大微波，并想在光上实现同样效果。

items.en: Gordon Gould is generally credited with coining the acronym laser from light amplification by stimulated emission of radiation.
items.cn: 一般认为，戈登·古尔德在 1957 年用「受激辐射光放大」的英文首字母造出 laser 这一缩略词。

items.en: Schawlow and Townes published the optical principle that made a light maser practical.
items.cn: 1958 年，肖洛与汤斯发表了使「光激射器」可行的光学原理。

items.en: Theodore Maiman built the first working ruby laser, and the word quickly entered newspapers.
items.cn: 1960 年，梅曼造出第一台可工作的红宝石激光器，这个词随即进入报端。

items.en: Modern English uses laser for the beam, the device and the technology, and has derived the verb lase.
items.cn: 现代英语用 laser 指光束、装置和技术，并由此派生出动词 lase。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the acronym's relatives and its predecessor; the near-meaning group collects words for light and beams.
note.cn: 形近组收这个缩略词的派生形式与前身；近义组收表示光和光束的词。

entries.definition: The microwave predecessor of the laser, using the same amplification principle.
entries.definitionCN: 激光器的微波前身，使用同样的放大原理。

entries.definition: To emit laser light or to treat something with a laser.
entries.definitionCN: 发出激光，或用激光处理某物。

entries.definition: A form of eye surgery that reshapes the cornea with a laser.
entries.definitionCN: 用激光重塑角膜的一种眼科手术。

entries.definition: A directed line of light or other radiation.
entries.definitionCN: 定向射出的一束光或其他辐射。

entries.definition: A single line or narrow stream of light.
entries.definitionCN: 一条光线或一束很细的光。

entries.definition: Energy travelling through space, including light and heat.
entries.definitionCN: 在空间中传播的能量，包括光和热。

normalIntro.en: The word is an acronym, so its memory hooks are the scientific phrase behind it and the family of devices and uses built on it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是缩略词，所以记忆抓手是它背后的科学短语，以及由它构成的装置与用途词族。

normal.en: Laser stands for light amplification by stimulated emission of radiation, which is a description rather than a root.
normal.cn: laser 代表「受激辐射光放大」，这是一句描述，而不是一个词根。

normal.en: The term was coined in 1957, which makes laser far younger than most words in this book.
normal.cn: 这个词造于 1957 年，因此比本书中大多数词年轻得多。

normal.en: Maser is the microwave older sibling; replace the m with l and the same idea becomes light.
normal.cn: maser 是它在微波波段的前身；把 m 换成 l，同一个想法就变成了光。

normal.en: Lase is a back-formation from laser, created by speakers who needed a verb for producing the beam.
normal.cn: lase 是从 laser 逆构出的动词，由需要表达「发出光束」的人造出来。

normal.en: Laser beam, laser printer and laser surgery are compounds that show the device spreading into new fields.
normal.cn: laser beam、laser printer 和 laser surgery 这些复合词显示装置正扩散到新的领域。

abstract.en: A word made from initials reminds us that language keeps building new roots out of new science.
abstract.cn: 由首字母造出的词提醒人：语言一直在用新科学搭建新的词根。

abstract.en: Light that is forced into one orderly direction becomes a tool, which is why the beam and the device share a name.
abstract.cn: 被约束到同一方向的光成了工具，所以光束与装置共用同一个名字。

abstract.en: Laser shows a technology so vivid that its acronym stops sounding like an acronym and starts feeling like a word.
abstract.cn: laser 说明一种技术足够鲜明，以至于它的缩略词不再像缩略词，而开始像一个普通单词。

examples.en: The laser cut through the metal sheet in seconds.
examples.cn: 激光几秒钟就切穿了金属板。

examples.en: The lab bought a new laser for the experiment.
examples.cn: 实验室为这项实验买了一台新的激光器。

examples.en: Laser is now common in eye surgery.
examples.cn: 激光如今在眼科手术中很常见。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「镭射」——这是 laser 的音译说法，指激光；记住 laser 就是激光。

root: 二十世纪缩略词，由「受激辐射光放大」这一科学短语的英文首字母组成，没有拉丁语或日耳曼语词根。

sensesIntro.en: The core is coherent light; the senses divide into the beam, the machine that makes it, and the technology built around it.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是高度一致的光；义项由此分为光束、制造光束的机器，以及围绕它形成的技术。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin red line of light leaving a machine and crossing the air without spreading.
core.cn: 核心意象：一束细红线从机器射出，穿过空气而不散开。

branches.en: a thin red line crossing a dark room
branches.cn: 暗室里划过的一道细红线

branches.en: a boxy machine humming on a lab bench
branches.cn: 实验台上嗡嗡作响的方形机器

branches.en: a surgeon's hand guided by a pencil of light
branches.cn: 一束笔直的光引导着外科医生的手

branches.en: a factory floor where metal is cut without a blade
branches.cn: 不用刀片就能切开金属的车间

branches.en: a cat chasing a moving dot from a laser pointer
branches.cn: 猫追着激光笔投下的移动小点

intro.en: The word is an acronym whose parts are ordinary English scientific terms; its later compounds and suffixes grow from the whole acronym.
intro.cn: 这个词是缩略词，其组成是普通的英语科学术语；后来的复合词与后缀则从整个缩略词上生长出来。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_en: final in order, the most recent, or to continue for a time

intro.en: Later is the comparative of late, an Old English adjective for slow and tardy that shifted its centre to time.
intro.cn: later 是 late 的比较级；late 是古英语中表示「慢、迟」的形容词，后来重心转到时间上。

items.en: The word belongs to a Germanic family that also gives German lass and the idea of letting go.
items.cn: 这个词属于日耳曼语族，同族还包括德语 lass 以及「放开」的概念。

items.en: The old comparative ending -ra produced lætra, the ancestor of later.
items.cn: 古老的比较级词尾 -ra 造出 lætra，即 later 的祖先。

items.en: Middle English later is fixed as the comparative of late and begins to work as an adverb.

items.en: Modern English adds the fixed phrases later on and sooner or later.
items.cn: 现代英语添上 later on 与 sooner or later 这类固定短语。

senses.title: Angular distance from the equator
senses.titleCN: 纬度：相对赤道的南北角距离
senses.definition: the angular distance of a place north or south of the equator, measured in degrees
senses.definitionCN: 某地相对赤道向南或向北的角距离，以度数计
senses.example: The island lies at a latitude of twenty degrees north.
senses.exampleCN: 这座岛屿位于北纬二十度。
senses.why: Latin latitudo meant 'breadth'; on a globe the north-south breadth of the known world became an angle measured from the equator.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 latitudo 意为「宽度」；在地球仪上，已知世界的南北「宽度」变成了从赤道量起的角度。

senses.title: A region or band of the globe
senses.titleCN: 纬度地区：由纬度划出的地带
senses.definition: a region of the earth identified by the latitude it occupies
senses.definitionCN: 按所占纬度来指认的地球区域
senses.example: Coffee grows well in the warm latitudes near the equator.
senses.exampleCN: 咖啡在赤道附近的温暖纬度带生长良好。
senses.why: Instead of a number, the word can name the band that the number marks, so 'the warm latitudes' means a zone, not a coordinate.
senses.whyCN: 这个词不只给数字，也能指数字所标出的地带，因此 the warm latitudes 指一片区域而非坐标。

senses.title: Freedom to act or decide
senses.titleCN: 自由度：行动与决定的余地
senses.definition: the freedom to choose how to act within a framework of rules
senses.definitionCN: 在规则框架内选择如何行动的自由
senses.example: The new editor was given wide latitude in choosing stories.
senses.exampleCN: 新编辑在选题上获得了很大的自由空间。
senses.why: A map coordinate can move within a range without leaving the map; freedom of action was pictured the same way, as room to move.
senses.whyCN: 地图坐标可以在范围内移动而不越出图幅；行动自由被同样地想象成可活动的余量。

senses.title: Permitted range or tolerance
senses.titleCN: 容许范围：可偏离的限度
senses.definition: the amount by which something may vary without breaking a rule or standard
senses.definitionCN: 某事物在不违反规则或标准的前提下可偏离的幅度
senses.example: The specification allows a latitude of two millimetres in the cut.
senses.exampleCN: 规格允许切割有两毫米的偏差。
senses.why: From room to move comes room to deviate: a tolerance is latitude expressed as an allowed error.
senses.whyCN: 由「可活动」引申出「可偏离」：公差就是把余地换算成允许的误差。

senses.title: Exposure latitude in photography
senses.titleCN: 曝光宽容度：底片可容忍的曝光范围
senses.definition: the range of exposure over which a film or sensor still gives a usable image
senses.definitionCN: 胶片或传感器仍能给出可用影像的曝光范围
senses.example: Negative film has more exposure latitude than slide film.
senses.exampleCN: 负片的曝光宽容度比反转片大。
senses.why: A photographic emulsion tolerates a range of light before it fails, exactly the 'permitted range' sense applied to light.
senses.whyCN: 感光乳剂在失效前能容忍一定范围的光量，正是「容许范围」义用于光线。

senses.title: Breadth or width, archaic
senses.titleCN: 宽度：横向量度（古义、技术义）
senses.definition: the breadth or width of a thing, now chiefly technical or historical
senses.definitionCN: 事物的横向宽度，今多用于技术或历史语境
senses.example: The old survey recorded the latitude of the field as forty paces.
senses.exampleCN: 旧时的测量记录这块地的宽度为四十步。
senses.why: This is the original Latin sense of latitudo 'breadth', preserved after the geographical sense took over everyday use.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁 latitudo「宽度」的本义，在地理义占据日常用法之后仍被保留。

senses.title: Lines of latitude on a map
senses.titleCN: 纬线：地图上与赤道平行的圈
senses.definition: a circle on a map or globe parallel to the equator, joining places of equal latitude
senses.definitionCN: 地图或地球仪上与赤道平行、连接同纬度各点的圈
senses.example: The chart draws lines of latitude every ten degrees.
senses.exampleCN: 这张海图每隔十度画一条纬线。
senses.why: The parallel is the visible mark of the measured angle, so 'latitude' can name the line as well as the number.
senses.whyCN: 纬线是所量角度的可见标记，因此 latitude 既可指数值也可指这条线。

senses.title: Celestial latitude
senses.titleCN: 黄纬：天体相对黄道的角距离
senses.definition: the angular distance of a celestial body north or south of the ecliptic
senses.definitionCN: 天体相对黄道向北或向南的角距离
senses.example: Astronomers record the celestial latitude of each planet.
senses.exampleCN: 天文学家记录每颗行星的黄纬。
senses.why: The same 'breadth' geometry was transferred to the sky, where the ecliptic serves as the baseline instead of the equator.
senses.whyCN: 同一套「宽度」几何被搬到天上，只是基准由赤道换成了黄道。

intro.en: Latitude comes from Latin latitudo 'breadth, width', formed on latus 'broad'. The geographical sense is a later narrowing of that breadth to an angular distance. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: latitude 来自拉丁 latitudo「宽度、广度」，由 latus「宽的」构成；地理义是后来把「广度」收窄为角距离。年代均为约数。

items.en: Latus meant 'broad, wide'; it is not the same word as latus, lateris 'side', although the two forms look alike in Latin dictionaries.
items.cn: latus 意为「宽的、广的」；它与 latus, lateris「侧边」并非同一个词，尽管在拉丁词典里两个词形相近。

items.en: Latus plus -tudo gave latitudo, 'breadth, width, extent'.
items.cn: latus 加 -tudo 构成 latitudo，意为「宽度、广度、范围」。

items.en: In sixteenth-century geography the 'breadth' of the known world became the north-south angular distance from the equator, the modern sense.
items.cn: 16 世纪地理学把已知世界的「广度」定为相对赤道的南北角距离，即现代义。

items.en: The same word was applied to the sky, where celestial latitude measures distance from the ecliptic rather than from the equator.
items.cn: 同一个词被用于天空，黄纬量的是相对黄道而非赤道的距离。

items.en: From the idea of a range or extent came the senses 'freedom of action' and 'permitted tolerance' in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.
items.cn: 从「范围、幅度」的观念引申出 16 至 17 世纪的「行动自由」与「容许误差」两义。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates only): the photographic sense is twentieth-century, and no precise first citation is recorded for it; the Latin root is well established.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：摄影义属 20 世纪，确切的最早书证未见记载；拉丁词根则已确立。

note.en: Group one holds the four -tude words most often confused on maps and in exams; group two holds words about range, room and breadth.
note.cn: 第一组是最容易在地图与考试中混淆的四个 -tude 词；第二组是关于范围、余地与宽度的词。

entries.definition: From longus 'long': the east-west coordinate, measured from a prime meridian, not from the equator.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 longus「长」：相对本初子午线量出的东西坐标，不以赤道为基准。

entries.definition: From altus 'high': vertical height above a reference level, whether of land or an aircraft.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 altus「高」：相对某基准的垂直高度，可指陆地或飞机。

entries.definition: A settled way of thinking or a bodily posture; its Latin source is aptitudo's neighbour actitudo, not latus.
entries.definitionCN: 指固定的想法或身体姿态；其拉丁来源是 actitudo，与 latus 无关。

entries.definition: From aptus 'fit': the capacity to learn or do something, with no geographic sense.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 aptus「合适」：学习或做某事的能力，不含地理意义。

entries.definition: The east-west angle paired with latitude to fix a position on the globe.
entries.definitionCN: 与纬度配对、用于确定地球位置的东西向角度。

entries.definition: The range covered by a plan, rule or activity; latitude adds the idea of permitted freedom.
entries.definitionCN: 计划、规则或活动覆盖的范围；latitude 另带「被允许的自由」之意。

entries.definition: The permitted variation in a measurement or in behaviour; latitude is the older, broader word for such room.
entries.definitionCN: 测量或行为上被允许的偏差；latitude 是更旧、更宽的说法。

entries.definition: The literal width of something; it is the original sense that latitude carried in Latin.
entries.definitionCN: 事物实际的宽度；正是 latitude 在拉丁语中携带的本义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Latin 'breadth', real map lines and real figurative uses, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁「宽度」、真实的地图线条与真实的比喻用法，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latus 'broad' + -tude 'state': the breadth of the world, later measured as an angle from the equator.
normal.cn: latus「宽」+ -tude「状态」：世界的广度，后来变成从赤道量起的角度。

normal.en: Latitude lines run east-west and measure north-south position; longitude lines do the opposite.
normal.cn: 纬线东西走向，却量南北位置；经线正好相反。

normal.en: The pair 'latitude and longitude' fixes any point on the globe.
normal.cn: 纬度与经度这一对数值能定位地球上的任何一点。

normal.en: Giving someone latitude means giving them room to choose within limits.
normal.cn: give someone latitude 指在限定的范围内给对方选择的余地。

normal.en: Film photographers speak of exposure latitude, the range of light a negative can survive.
normal.cn: 胶片摄影师说曝光宽容度，即负片能承受的光量范围。

abstract.en: Picture a rubber band that can stretch only so far before it snaps.
abstract.cn: 想象一根橡皮筋，拉到一定程度就会断。

abstract.en: Picture a map with many horizontal belts, each one a different warmth.
abstract.cn: 想象一张地图上有许多水平地带，每一带温度不同。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler laid across the globe rather than along it.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺横着放在地球上，而不是沿着地表。

examples.en: The ship's latitude was forty degrees south.
examples.cn: 这艘船的纬度是南纬四十度。

examples.en: Teachers are given latitude in how they organise their lessons.
examples.cn: 教师在如何组织课程上享有自主空间。

examples.en: Warm latitudes support a greater variety of plants.
examples.cn: 温暖的纬度带能养活更多种类的植物。

dict_mnemonic.text: lat（宽，如 lateral 侧面的、latitudes 纬度）+ itude（状态）→ 地球的横向宽度 → 纬度、余地

root: 拉丁 latitudo「宽度」= latus「宽的」+ -tudo（状态）；与 latus, lateris「侧边」不是同一个词。英语 latitude 经法语借入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses grow from one Latin idea, 'breadth': the globe's north-south breadth, the bands it creates, the room a person has to act, the error a standard allows, the light a film tolerates, literal width, the drawn parallel, and the sky's version of the same measure.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从拉丁「宽度」这一观念长出：地球的南北广度、由此划出的地带、人可行动的余地、标准允许的误差、胶片可容忍的光量、字面的宽度、画出的纬线，以及天空中的同一量度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a band stretched across a sphere, wide in the north-south direction, then read as an angle.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条横跨球面的带子，在南北方向上有宽度，再被读成角度。

branches.en: MEASURE AND MARK: the angle and the parallel line are the number and its visible trace.
branches.cn: 测量与标记：角度与纬线，是数值与它的可见痕迹。

branches.en: BANDS OF THE SPHERE: one band is on the earth, the other is projected onto the sky.
branches.cn: 球面上的带：一带在地球上，另一带投影到天空。

branches.en: ROOM: freedom to act and tolerance in a standard are the same slack measured in behaviour and in numbers.
branches.cn: 余地：行动自由与标准公差，是同一段松紧在行为与数字上的度量。

branches.en: LIGHT: a film's exposure latitude is the permitted range applied to light.
branches.cn: 光：胶片的曝光宽容度就是把容许范围用于光线。

branches.en: LITERAL WIDTH: the oldest sense survives as a technical word for breadth.
branches.cn: 字面宽度：最古老的意义作为表示宽度的技术词留存下来。

intro.en: Latitude is built on a Latin adjective for 'broad' plus a state suffix; the same root also appears in dilate, where the idea of widening is physical.
intro.cn: latitude 由表示「宽」的拉丁形容词加状态后缀构成；同一词根也出现在 dilate 中，那里「变宽」是物理动作。

latinIntro.en: Latin latus 'broad' gives latitudo and latitude; the verb dilatare 'to spread out' comes from dis- plus latus and yields dilate, dilation and dilatory.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 latus「宽」衍生 latitudo 与 latitude；动词 dilatare「摊开」由 dis- 加 latus 构成，衍生 dilate、dilation 与 dilatory。

items.example: The root names extent across, not length along.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根指横向的幅度，而非纵向的长度。

items.example: The latitude of the site is marked in degrees.
items.exampleCN: 该地点的纬度以度数标注。

items.example: The forest changes along a latitudinal gradient.

items.meaning: a person who allows broad interpretation
items.example: The latitudinarian clergy avoided strict tests.
items.exampleCN: 宽容派教士避免严格的信条审查。

items.example: The pupil dilates in dim light.
Dilation of the blood vessel improved flow.
The dilatory reply cost them the contract.
items.exampleCN: 拖延的答复让他们失去了合同。

definition_zh: 笑；笑声
definition_en: the act or sound of laughing
core_image: 一群人的笑声同时从屋里涌出来，像一阵轻快的风
scene: 客厅里有人讲了个笨拙的笑话，满屋的人一起笑出声。Her laughter filled the small kitchen.
sceneCN: 这里是「笑声」（第 1 个义项：笑的声音或行为）；句意为她的笑声充满了小厨房。图中可辨识物件：客厅、围坐的人、冒着热气的杯子。

derivatives.zh: laughter 的词根动词，义为「笑；笑声」
由 laugh 加 -able 构成，义为「可笑的；荒唐的」
由 laugh 加 -ing 构成，义为「笑着的；带笑的」

senses.title: The sound of laughing
senses.definition: the sound made when people laugh, often heard as a whole rather than word by word
senses.definitionCN: 人们笑时发出的声音，通常作为一个整体被听见
senses.example: Her laughter filled the small kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 她的笑声充满了小厨房。
senses.why: Laughter is the old noun beside the verb laugh; it names the sound itself, the way thunder names the noise rather than the flash.
senses.whyCN: laughter 是动词 laugh 旁边的古老名词，指声音本身，就像 thunder 指雷声而不是闪电。

senses.title: Amusement shown by laughing
senses.definition: the expression of amusement or joy through laughing, considered as a shared response
senses.definitionCN: 通过笑表现出来的愉悦或快乐，被视为一种共同的反应
senses.example: The room was full of laughter after the story.
senses.exampleCN: 故事讲完后，屋里满是欢笑。
senses.why: Because laughter is heard, it can stand for the whole mood of a group, not only for one person's sound.
senses.whyCN: 因为笑声是听得见的，它能代表一群人的整体气氛，而不只是某一个人的声音。

intro.en: Laughter is an Old English noun built beside the verb laugh, and the pair has stayed together for a thousand years.
intro.cn: laughter 是古英语中与动词 laugh 并列构成的名词，这一对词已经一起走了一千年。

items.en: Hleahter was the noun for laughter, formed from the verb hliehhan.
items.cn: hleahter 是表示「笑」的名词，由动词 hliehhan 构成。

items.en: The Germanic root also gives German lachen and Dutch lachen, all meaning to laugh.
items.cn: 同一日耳曼词根也给出德语 lachen 与荷兰语 lachen，都表示「笑」。

items.en: Middle English laughter keeps the noun while the verb settles into laugh.
items.cn: 中古英语保留名词 laughter，而动词固定为 laugh。

items.en: The spelling with -gh- becomes standard, matching the verb in the same period.
items.cn: 带 -gh- 的拼写在十六世纪成为标准，与同一时期的动词拼写一致。

items.en: Modern English keeps laughter almost unchanged, often in fixed phrases such as burst into laughter.
items.cn: 现代英语中 laughter 几乎未变，常出现在 burst into laughter 这样的固定短语里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the laugh family; the near-meaning group gathers sounds and moods of amusement.
note.cn: 形近组收 laugh 词族；近义组收表示愉快声音与情绪的词。

entries.definition: To make the sound of amusement, or that sound.
entries.definitionCN: 笑；笑声。

entries.definition: Making the sound of laughter.
entries.definitionCN: 笑着的；带笑的。

entries.definition: So silly that it deserves laughter.
entries.definitionCN: 可笑的；荒唐的。

entries.definition: While laughing, or in a joking way.
entries.definitionCN: 笑着地；开玩笑地。

entries.definition: A light, silly laugh.
entries.definitionCN: 咯咯笑；傻笑。

entries.definition: A quiet laugh with the mouth closed.
entries.definitionCN: 低声轻笑。

entries.definition: Great amusement expressed in laughter.
entries.definitionCN: 欢乐；欢笑。

entries.definition: The feeling of finding something funny.
entries.definitionCN: 愉悦；好笑。

normalIntro.en: The noun is inseparable from its verb, and its suffix is the old -ter that turns an action into a thing heard.
normalIntro.cn: 这个名词与它的动词不可分割，后缀是古老的 -ter，把动作变成听得见的东西。

normal.en: Laughter is the noun beside the verb laugh, not a separate word.
normal.cn: laughter 是动词 laugh 旁边的名词，不是另一个词。

normal.en: The ending -ter appears in other old nouns of action, such as laughter and slaughter.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ter 也出现在其他古老的动作名词里，如 laughter 与 slaughter。

normal.en: Burst into laughter is the common phrase for a sudden start.
normal.cn: burst into laughter 是表示「突然笑出声」的常用搭配。

normal.en: Laughter is uncountable: a burst of laughter, not a laughter.
normal.cn: laughter 不可数：说 a burst of laughter，不说 a laughter。

normal.en: The -gh- is silent, just as in laugh.
normal.cn: 其中的 -gh- 不发音，和 laugh 一样。

abstract.en: A sound can become a noun and then stand for a whole mood, which is how laughter fills a room.
abstract.cn: 一种声音可以变成名词，再代表一整个气氛，laughter 就是这样「充满」一个房间的。

abstract.en: English keeps both laugh and laughter so that the act and the sound can be named separately.
abstract.cn: 英语同时保留 laugh 与 laughter，让动作与声音可以分开命名。

abstract.en: Laughter is shared by definition: it is made to be heard.
abstract.cn: laughter 天生是共享的：它被制造出来就是为了让人听见。

examples.en: Her laughter filled the small kitchen.
examples.cn: 她的笑声充满了小厨房。

examples.en: The room was full of laughter after the story.
examples.cn: 故事讲完后，屋里满是欢笑。

examples.en: He burst into laughter at the sight.
examples.cn: 看到那一幕，他突然大笑起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拉夫特」——笑到拉长了脸的特效，就是 laughter。

root: 古英语 hleahter（笑声），由动词 hliehhan（笑）构成，属日耳曼语族。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the heard sound of laughing; it extends from one person's laugh to the shared mood of a group.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是听得见的笑的声音；由一个人的笑扩展到一群人的共同气氛。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wave of laughter rolling out of a room and over the listeners.
core.cn: 核心意象：一阵笑声从屋里涌出，盖过听的人。

branches.en: three notes of laughter from the next room
branches.cn: 隔壁传来的几声笑

branches.en: a joke that ends in a table of laughter
branches.cn: 以满桌笑声收尾的笑话

branches.en: a party where laughter replaces talk
branches.cn: 笑声代替谈话的聚会

branches.en: a memory kept as a sound rather than a picture
branches.cn: 以声音而非画面留下的记忆

branches.en: one sound that becomes the whole room
branches.cn: 一种声音变成整个房间

intro.en: An Old English noun, its verb, and the old suffix -ter make the core of this small family.
intro.cn: 一个古英语名词、它的动词，以及古老的后缀 -ter 构成这个小词族的核心。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: to make the sound of amusement
an action made into a thing
items.meaningCN: 把动作变成名词的词尾

definition_zh: 发射；发起；推出；（船）下水；发射活动；（产品的）发布
definition_en: to send a ship, rocket or product into motion or into the market, and the act of starting something new
core_image: 船坞闸门打开，新船顺着滑道冲向水面
scene: 码头上挤满了来看新船下水的人。The yard will launch the new ferry at dawn.
sceneCN: 这里 launch 指「使船下水」（第 1 个义项）；句意为船厂将在黎明时让新渡轮下水。图中可辨识物件：船坞闸门、滑道、围观的人群。

collocations.phrase: the launch of a new service

derivatives.zh: 由 launch 加 -er 构成，指发射装置或发射者
由 launch 与 pad 复合，指发射台、起飞平台
由 re- 加 launch 构成，指重新推出、再次发起

senses.title: To send a newly built ship into the water
senses.definition: to move a newly built boat from the slipway into the water for the first time
senses.definitionCN: 把新造的船第一次从滑道送入水中
senses.example: The yard will launch the new ferry at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 船厂将在黎明时让新渡轮下水。
senses.why: The word began as a lance thrown forward, so the first maritime use pictured a hull driven down a slipway like a weapon released.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指向前掷出的长矛，因此最早的船舶用法把船体沿滑道冲下，想象成一件被放出的武器。

senses.title: To start an activity, company or product
senses.definition: to begin something new such as a business, a campaign or a product, and make it public
senses.definitionCN: 开始并公开推出企业、运动或产品等新事物
senses.example: The company will launch its new phone next month.
senses.exampleCN: 公司下个月将推出新手机。
senses.why: Starting a venture is like setting a ship afloat: both release something built in private into the open, where it must stay afloat on its own.
senses.whyCN: 开创一项事业就像让船下水：两者都把在内部造好的东西放出去，此后它必须自己浮在水面上。

senses.title: To send a rocket or spacecraft into the air
senses.definition: to send a rocket, missile or spacecraft up into the sky or into space
senses.definitionCN: 把火箭、导弹或航天器送上天空或太空
senses.example: They launched the satellite from a desert site.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在沙漠场地发射了那颗卫星。
senses.why: A rocket is thrown upward the way a lance was thrown, and the old image of a forceful release fits the modern machine exactly.
senses.whyCN: 火箭被向上抛出，正如长矛被掷出，那个「用力放出」的旧画面恰好贴合现代机器。

senses.title: The act of launching something
senses.definition: the event or act of starting, releasing or putting something into service, used as a noun
senses.definitionCN: 启动、放出或让某物投入使用的活动，作名词
senses.example: The launch of the new service was covered by every paper.
senses.exampleCN: 新服务的发布被各家报纸报道。
senses.why: English often turns a forceful verb into a noun, so the moment of release becomes a public event with guests and speeches.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把有力的动词变成名词，于是「放出的那一刻」成了有来宾和致辞的公开活动。

intro.en: Launch goes back to a Latin word for a spear, and the idea of hurling something forward runs through all of its senses.
intro.cn: launch 可追到拉丁语中表示长矛的词，而「把东西向前掷出」这个意思贯穿它的所有义项。

items.en: Lancea meant a light spear, the weapon carried by a lancer.
items.cn: lancea 指轻矛，是长矛手使用的武器。

items.en: Lanceare meant to wield a lance, and in French the sense widened to throwing or driving something forward.
items.cn: lanceare 意为挥动长矛，在法语中词义扩大到把东西向前投出或推动。

items.en: Old French lanchier meant to hurl a spear or to set a boat afloat, and English borrowed both ideas.
items.cn: 古法语 lanchier 意为投掷矛枪或让船下水，英语把这两种意思都借了过来。

items.en: Middle English launch kept the movement sense: to let something go forward, whether a boat, a weapon or a shout.
items.cn: 中古英语 launch 保留「向前放出」的意思：无论是船、武器还是一声喊。

items.en: Modern English extended the word from ships to rockets and businesses, so launch now starts almost anything.
items.cn: 现代英语把词义从船扩展到火箭与企业，于是 launch 几乎能「启动」任何东西。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the lance family and its built forms; the near-meaning group collects verbs for beginning or releasing something.
note.cn: 形近组收 lance 一词族及其构成形式；近义组收表示开始或放出的动词。

entries.definition: A device or person that sends something into the air.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物送上天空的装置或人。

entries.definition: The platform from which a rocket leaves the ground.
entries.definitionCN: 火箭升空所依托的平台。

entries.definition: A long spear, the weapon behind the word.
entries.definitionCN: 长矛，是这个词背后的武器。

entries.definition: To begin doing or making something.
entries.definitionCN: 开始做或开始制造某物。

entries.definition: To set a process or plan going.
entries.definitionCN: 启动一个过程或计划。

entries.definition: To let something go out or become available.
entries.definitionCN: 放出某物或使其可获取。

entries.definition: To shoot a weapon or set off a rocket.
entries.definitionCN: 射击武器或点火发射火箭。

normalIntro.en: A spear thrown forward is the oldest picture inside this word, and every later sense repeats the same release.
normalIntro.cn: 一支向前掷出的长矛是这个词里最古老的画面，此后每个义项都在重复同一次「放出」。

normal.en: Latin lancea is a spear, and lanceare means to use one, which is the physical core of launch.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 lancea 是长矛，lanceare 是使用长矛，这就是 launch 的物理核心。

normal.en: A ship is launched down a slipway, driven forward like a thrown weapon.
normal.cn: 船沿滑道下水，像被掷出的武器一样被推向前方。

normal.en: A product launch borrows the same gesture: something built inside is pushed out into the market.
normal.cn: 产品发布借用同一个动作：在内部造好的东西被推向市场。

normal.en: A rocket launch repeats the old throw upward, with fire instead of muscle.
normal.cn: 火箭发射重复了古老的向上投掷，只是用火代替了肌肉。

normal.en: Launcher and launchpad name the tool and the place that make the release possible.
normal.cn: launcher 与 launchpad 指让这次「放出」得以发生的工具和地点。

abstract.en: One verb covers ships, rockets and businesses because all three must leave the place where they were built.
abstract.cn: 一个动词涵盖船、火箭与企业，因为三者都必须离开自己被造出来的地方。

abstract.en: A launch is a public moment because release is risky: once it is out, it must float without help.
abstract.cn: 发布是公开的时刻，因为放出有风险：一旦出去，它必须自己浮着。

abstract.en: The lance became a satellite, but the gesture is still a throw.
abstract.cn: 长矛变成了卫星，可那个动作仍然是一次投掷。

examples.en: The yard will launch the new ferry at dawn.
examples.cn: 船厂将在黎明时让新渡轮下水。

examples.en: The company will launch its new phone next month.
examples.cn: 公司下个月将推出新手机。

examples.en: They launched the satellite from a desert site.
examples.cn: 他们在沙漠场地发射了那颗卫星。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「浪起」——浪头起来了，船就下水、火箭就升空；谐音记住 launch 是发射、发起。

root: 源自拉丁语 lancea（长矛）与 lanceare（挥矛），经古法语 lanchier（投矛、使船下水）进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The core image is something thrown forward; it becomes a ship sliding into water, a rocket rising, and a product sent into the market.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心意象是把东西向前掷出；它化为滑入水中的船、升空的火箭，以及推向市场的产品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: dock gates open and a new hull slides down the slipway into the water.
core.cn: 核心意象：船坞闸门打开，新船体沿滑道冲入水中。

branches.en: a hull sliding down greased timbers
branches.cn: 船体沿涂油的木滑道下滑

branches.en: a crowd watching a ferry enter the water
branches.cn: 人群看着渡轮入水

branches.en: a phone shown on a stage for the first time
branches.cn: 手机第一次在台上亮相

branches.en: a rocket clearing the tower
branches.cn: 火箭飞离发射塔

branches.en: newspapers reporting a service launch
branches.cn: 报纸报道一项服务的发布

intro.en: A Latin spear and its verb pass through French into English, and English adds -er and a compound to name the tools of release.
intro.cn: 拉丁语的「矛」及其动词经法语进入英语，英语又加 -er 和复合成分来命名放出的工具。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 待洗的衣物；洗衣房；洗衣店；洗衣
definition_en: clothes and sheets that need washing or have just been washed; a place or business where they are washed; the work of washing them
core_image: 堆在篮子里的衬衫、毛巾和床单，旁边是一台洗衣机
scene: 周末的早上，装满脏衣服的篮子放在洗衣机旁，主人却一直没有动手。The basket of laundry sat beside the washing machine all weekend.
sceneCN: 这里是「待洗的衣物」（第 1 个义项：需要清洗的织物）；句意是那篮待洗的衣物整个周末都放在洗衣机旁。图中可辨识物件：洗衣篮、衬衫、洗衣机。

pos.zh: 待洗的衣物；洗衣房；洗衣店；洗衣

collocations.zh: 脏衣服；不可告人的丑事

derivatives.zh: 由 laundry 去掉名词后缀 -ry 逆构而成，义为「洗熨衣物；洗钱」
由 launder 加表示「小型场所」的后缀 -ette 构成，义为「自助洗衣店」
由 launder 加表示「女性从业者」的后缀 -ess 构成，义为「洗衣妇」

senses.title: Clothes and linen that need washing
senses.definition: clothes, sheets and other household linen that need washing or have just been washed
senses.definitionCN: 需要清洗或刚刚洗好的衣服、床单等家用织物
senses.example: The basket of laundry sat beside the washing machine all weekend.
senses.exampleCN: 那篮待洗的衣物整个周末都放在洗衣机旁。
senses.why: The Old French source named the place and the store of things to be washed, and English first used the word for that heap of cloth.
senses.whyCN: 古法语来源既指场所，也指待洗的一堆东西，英语最初便用这个词指那堆织物。

senses.title: A room or shop where clothes are washed
senses.definition: a room in a house, or a shop, where clothes are washed
senses.definitionCN: 住宅内的洗衣房间，或专门清洗衣物的店铺
senses.example: He took his shirts to the laundry on the corner.
senses.exampleCN: 他把衬衫送到街角的洗衣店。
senses.why: The word first named the place where washing happened, and that place sense survives beside the heap of clothes.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指洗衣发生的场所，而这个场所义一直与那堆衣物并存。

senses.title: The work or business of washing clothes
senses.definition: the activity or trade of washing clothes and linen
senses.definitionCN: 清洗衣物与织物的活动或行业
senses.example: Laundry is the one chore she never puts off.
senses.exampleCN: 洗衣服是她唯一不会拖延的家务。
senses.why: Because the place and the task were always linked, the word could also name the activity itself, much as cook gave cooking.
senses.whyCN: 由于场所与任务始终相连，这个词也能指活动本身，就像 cook 派生出 cooking 一样。

intro.en: Laundry comes from a Latin verb for washing by way of French; the place, the clothes and the task have shared the word for centuries.
intro.cn: laundry 由拉丁语「洗」的动词经法语传来；场所、衣物与洗衣这件事共用这个词已有数百年。

items.en: The Latin verb lavare meant to wash, and it also underlies words such as lavatory.
items.cn: 拉丁语动词 lavare 意为洗，lavatory 等词也由它派生。

items.en: Late Latin lavandaria named things to be washed or a place for washing them.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 lavandaria 指待洗之物或清洗它们的场所。

items.en: Old French lavanderie named the place where washing was done and the household linen handled there.
items.cn: 古法语 lavanderie 指洗衣的场所，也指在那里处理的家庭织物。

items.en: Middle English lavendrie lost the first v and moved towards the modern shape laundry.
items.cn: 中古英语 lavendrie 丢掉第一个 v，逐渐向现代形式 laundry 靠拢。

items.en: Modern English uses laundry for the clothes, the room or shop, and the work itself.
items.cn: 现代英语用 laundry 指衣物、洗衣房间或店铺，也指洗衣这件事。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the verb and the people and places built on it; the near-meaning group collects words for cloth and cleaning.
note.cn: 形近组收由它派生的动词、人和场所；近义组收表示织物与清洁的词。

entries.definition: To wash and iron clothes, or to move money through a legitimate business.
entries.definitionCN: 洗熨衣物；也指通过合法生意洗钱。

entries.definition: A self-service laundry with coin-operated machines.
entries.definitionCN: 设有投币机器的自助洗衣店。

entries.definition: A woman whose job was to wash clothes.
entries.definitionCN: 以洗衣为业的妇女。

entries.definition: A toilet or washroom; it shares the Latin verb for washing.
entries.definitionCN: 厕所或洗手间；与 laundry 共用拉丁语「洗」的动词。

entries.definition: Clothes that are being washed or have just been washed.
entries.definitionCN: 正在洗或刚洗好的衣物。

entries.definition: Sheets, tablecloths and similar household cloth.
entries.definitionCN: 床单、桌布一类的家用织物。

entries.definition: Items worn on the body, whether clean or dirty.
entries.definitionCN: 穿在身上的衣物，无论干净与否。

entries.definition: A washing method that uses chemicals rather than water.
entries.definitionCN: 用化学溶剂而非水来清洁衣物的方法。

normalIntro.en: The family hangs on a Latin verb for washing, and English suffixes turn it into a shop, a worker and a verb.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词族挂在拉丁语表示「洗」的动词上，英语后缀又把它变成店铺、从业者和动词。

normal.en: Laundry goes back to Latin lavare, to wash, the same verb behind lavatory and lavation.
normal.cn: laundry 可追溯到拉丁语 lavare「洗」，lavatory 与 lavation 也出自同一个动词。

normal.en: Launder is the verb formed from the noun, and it now also means to wash dirty money clean.
normal.cn: launder 是从名词变出的动词，如今也指把来路不干净的钱「洗」干净。

normal.en: Launderette is a small self-service laundry, with -ette marking a compact place.
normal.cn: launderette 是小型自助洗衣店，后缀 -ette 标记一个较小的场所。

normal.en: Laundress is the old word for a woman who washed clothes, with -ess marking a female worker.
normal.cn: laundress 是旧时指洗衣妇女的词，后缀 -ess 标记女性从业者。

normal.en: Laundry basket is the place where the heap waits, which is why the word can mean both the heap and the task.
normal.cn: laundry basket 是那堆衣物等待的地方，所以这个词既能指那堆衣物，也能指洗衣这件事。

abstract.en: A word that means the clothes, the room and the work shows how domestic labour blurs object and action.
abstract.cn: 一个同时指衣物、房间和工作的词，说明家务劳动如何把物件与动作混在一起。

abstract.en: Clean water is the hidden subject of laundry, just as it is of so much household life.
abstract.cn: 干净的水是 laundry 背后隐藏的主题，正如它在许多家庭生活中那样。

abstract.en: Laundry waits in a basket until someone decides to begin, which makes it a small picture of unfinished time.
abstract.cn: 衣物在篮子里等着有人决定开始，这使它成为未完成时间的一幅小图。

examples.en: The basket of laundry sat beside the washing machine all weekend.
examples.cn: 那篮待洗的衣物整个周末都放在洗衣机旁。

examples.en: He took his shirts to the laundry on the corner.
examples.cn: 他把衬衫送到街角的洗衣店。

examples.en: Laundry is the one chore she never puts off.
examples.cn: 洗衣服是她唯一不会拖延的家务。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「落恩缀」——脏衣服落进篮子，等着人去洗；laundry 是待洗的衣物。

root: 拉丁语 lavare（洗）→ 晚期拉丁语 lavandaria（待洗之物、洗衣处）→ 古法语 lavanderie → 中古英语 lavendrie → 现代英语 laundry。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the heap of cloth to be washed; the senses divide into the place where it is washed and the work of washing it.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是待洗的一堆织物；义项由此分为清洗它的场所和清洗这件事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a basket of shirts, towels and sheets beside a washing machine.
core.cn: 核心意象：洗衣机旁一篮衬衫、毛巾和床单。

branches.en: a heap of shirts waiting beside a machine
branches.cn: 机器旁等待的一堆衬衫

branches.en: a basket that stays full until Sunday night
branches.cn: 一直满到周日夜晚的洗衣篮

branches.en: a shop on the corner with rows of machines
branches.cn: 街角一排排机器的店铺

branches.en: a small room at the back of a house
branches.cn: 住宅后部的一间小屋

branches.en: a chore that begins with sorting and ends with folding
branches.cn: 从分类开始、以叠好结束的家务

intro.cn: 拉丁语表示「洗」的动词经法语进入英语，英语再用后缀造出动词、店铺和女性从业者。
