definition_zh: 熔岩；熔岩流；熔岩冷却形成的岩石；熔岩穹丘；熔岩管；枕状熔岩；比喻大量涌出之物；熔岩灯
definition_en: molten rock that has reached a planet's surface and flows from a volcano, or the solid rock it forms when it cools
core_image: 火山口边缘，暗红的黏稠流体沿斜坡推进，表面结出黑色硬壳，壳缝里透出橙色光
scene: 夜里的山坡上，暗红色流体一边移动一边结壳，缓慢逼近远处的房屋。 A river of lava cut across the road and reached the sea by dawn.
sceneCN: 这里 lava 指流出地表的熔岩（第 1 个义项：到达地表并正在流动的高温熔融岩石）；句意为一条熔岩流横穿公路，天亮时抵达海边。

pos.zh: 熔岩（到达地表的熔融岩石）
熔岩流；熔岩冷却形成的岩石
熔岩灯；（比喻）大量涌出之物

derivatives.zh: 熔岩的；似熔岩的（较少见，地质学用）
熔岩般的；像熔岩那样炽热流动的
熔岩流（复合术语，指流动的熔岩体及其堆积）
熔岩穹丘（复合术语，黏稠熔岩堆成的圆丘）
熔岩管（复合术语，熔岩流内部排空后留下的隧道）

senses.title: Molten rock at the surface
senses.definition: molten rock that has reached the surface through a vent
senses.definitionCN: 通过火山口到达地表的熔融岩石
senses.example: Lava poured from a fissure on the flank of the cone.
senses.exampleCN: 熔岩从锥体侧面的裂缝中涌出。
senses.why: lava names the melt only after it is exposed; while it is underground the same material is still magma.
senses.whyCN: lava 只在这团熔体露出地表之后才这么叫；它在地下时仍是 magma。

senses.title: A stream of lava
senses.definition: a flowing body of lava moving down a slope, or the deposit it leaves
senses.definitionCN: 沿坡面流动的熔岩体，或它留下的堆积物
senses.example: The lava flow stopped two hundred metres from the village.
senses.exampleCN: 熔岩流在离村庄两百米处停住。
senses.why: the moving stream became a countable thing, so the word can name one flow as well as the substance.
senses.whyCN: 流动的熔岩被当作可数的个体，于是该词既能指物质，也能指一条熔岩流。

senses.title: The rock that lava becomes
senses.definition: the solid igneous rock formed when a lava flow cools, commonly basalt
senses.definitionCN: 熔岩流冷却后形成的坚硬火成岩，常见为玄武岩
senses.example: The cliff is made of lava that hardened under water.
senses.exampleCN: 这道崖壁由在水下硬结的熔岩构成。
senses.why: once cooled, the material keeps the name of its molten stage, so the product inherits the word.
senses.whyCN: 冷却之后，这种材料仍沿用熔融阶段的名称，于是产物继承了该词。

senses.title: A dome of thick lava
senses.definition: a rounded mound built by viscous lava piling up around a vent
senses.definitionCN: 黏稠熔岩在火山口周围堆叠而成的圆丘
senses.example: The lava dome grew by several metres each week.
senses.exampleCN: 熔岩穹丘每周增高数米。
senses.why: stiff lava cannot run far, so it stacks into a dome, and the compound records that behaviour.
senses.whyCN: 黏稠的熔岩流不远，只能堆成穹丘，这个复合词记录了这种行为。

senses.title: A tube left by a lava flow
senses.definition: a hollow tunnel formed when the surface of a lava flow crusts over while the molten interior drains away
senses.definitionCN: 熔岩流表面结壳、内部熔体排空后留下的空心隧道
senses.example: The lava tube ran for six kilometres beneath the field.
senses.exampleCN: 这条熔岩管从田野下方延伸六公里。
senses.why: the crust freezes first, the interior keeps moving, and the empty channel survives as a tube.
senses.whyCN: 表层先凝固，内部继续流动，排空后的通道便作为管道留存。

senses.title: Pillow lava
senses.definition: bulbous, pillow-shaped masses of lava formed where lava is erupted under water
senses.definitionCN: 熔岩在水下喷出时形成的球状、枕状团块
senses.example: Pillow lava on the sea floor showed the eruption had been submarine.
senses.exampleCN: 海底的枕状熔岩表明这次喷发发生在水下。
senses.why: water chills the outside instantly, so each pulse of lava freezes as a rounded pillow.
senses.whyCN: 水使外层瞬间冷却，于是每一股熔岩都冻成圆枕状。

senses.title: A flood of something
senses.definition: a figurative use for something that pours out in great quantity, often hot or unstoppable
senses.definitionCN: 比喻大量涌出之物，常带灼热或不可阻挡的意味
senses.example: Lava of complaints poured into the office after the launch.
senses.exampleCN: 产品上线后，投诉如熔岩般涌进办公室。
senses.why: the image keeps heat and unstoppable flow, so the word suggests something that cannot be held back.
senses.whyCN: 这个意象保留了高温与不可阻挡的流动，因此暗示无法被拦住的东西。

senses.title: The lava lamp
senses.definition: a decorative lamp in which blobs of coloured wax rise and fall in heated liquid, named for their look
senses.definitionCN: 一种装饰灯，加热液体中彩色蜡块升降起伏，因其外观而得名
senses.example: A lava lamp glowed on the shelf beside the old record player.
senses.exampleCN: 旧唱机旁的架子上亮着一盏熔岩灯。
senses.why: the wax blobs mimic rising and sinking lava, so a cultural object borrowed the geological word.
senses.whyCN: 蜡块升降的样子模仿熔岩，于是一件文化物件借用了这个地质词。

intro.en: Lava entered English from Italian, specifically the Neapolitan dialect, where lava meant a torrent or stream. Its deeper origin is disputed: one common hypothesis links it to Latin labes, a fall or slide, from labi, to slip; others suggest Latin lavare, to wash, or a local pre-Roman word. It is not a direct Latin inheritance, and no single origin is settled.
intro.cn: lava 经意大利语、具体是那不勒斯方言进入英语，方言中 lava 指急流或水流。其更深来源有争议：一种常见假说把它联系到拉丁 labes「坠落、滑落」，出自 labi「滑落」；也有人提出拉丁 lavare「洗」，或当地前罗马时期的词。它不是拉丁语的直接继承词，也没有定论。

items.en: In the Naples dialect lava meant a torrent, especially a stream of rain water rushing down a slope.
items.cn: 在那不勒斯方言中，lava 指急流，尤指雨水沿坡冲下的水流。

items.en: One hypothesis derives the dialect word from Latin labes, a fall or sliding, from labi, to slip; the image of sliding material fits a lava flow, but the chain is unproven.
items.cn: 一种假说把方言词追溯到拉丁 labes「坠落、滑落」，出自 labi「滑落」；「滑落之物」的意象与熔岩流相合，但这条例证链未被证实。

items.en: Other suggestions connect lava to Latin lavare, to wash, or to a pre-Roman local word; scholars have not agreed, so no single origin is asserted here.
items.cn: 其他说法把 lava 联系到拉丁 lavare「洗」，或联系到前罗马时期的当地词；学界未达成一致，因此此处不指定单一来源。

items.en: English travellers and naturalists brought the word home in the eighteenth century, describing Vesuvius and Etna.
items.cn: 英语世界的旅行者与博物学家在十八世纪把这个词带回，用于描述维苏威火山与埃特纳火山。

items.en: Geology built a family of compounds: lava flow, lava dome, lava tube, pillow lava, each naming a shape the melt takes.
items.cn: 地质学构造了一族复合词：熔岩流、熔岩穹丘、熔岩管、枕状熔岩，各自指熔体的一种形态。

items.en: Source uncertain (root in doubt): the Italian route is well documented, but the deeper origin is unsettled; it is generally thought to be related to Latin labes, a fall, while lavare, to wash, and a pre-Roman local word are competing hypotheses, so no single source is chosen; the first English date is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根存疑）：意大利语这条路径有充分记录；但更深的来源未定，一般认为是与拉丁 labes「坠落」有关的假说，另有 lavare「洗」及前罗马时期当地词等说法并列，不选定论；英语首见的确切年代为约数。

note.en: Group one holds look-alike forms; group two holds the terms that overlap with lava in geology.
note.cn: 第一组是形近形式；第二组是在地质学中与熔岩重叠的术语。

entries.definition: The immature form of an insect or other animal; the spelling differs by a single letter and the meaning is unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 昆虫或其他动物的幼体；拼写只差一个字母，意义毫无关联。

entries.definition: A rare adjective meaning of or like lava, used mainly in geological writing.
entries.definitionCN: 少见形容词，意为熔岩的或似熔岩的，主要用于地质写作。

entries.definition: The regular plural, used when counting separate flows or types of melt.
entries.definitionCN: 规则复数，用于计数不同的熔岩流或熔岩类型。

entries.definition: The decorative lamp whose wax blobs suggested the name, now the best-known non-geological use.
entries.definitionCN: 那种蜡块让人联想到熔岩的装饰灯，如今是该词最知名的非地质用法。

entries.definition: The same molten rock before it reaches the surface; the two words mark stages, not different substances.
entries.definitionCN: 同一种熔融岩石在到达地表之前的名称；两词标记的是阶段，而非不同物质。

entries.definition: A neutral description of rock heated to liquid, avoiding the technical stage terms.
entries.definitionCN: 对加热成液态的岩石的中性描述，避开阶段术语。

entries.definition: The dark, fine-grained rock most lava flows become; it names the product after cooling.
entries.definitionCN: 多数熔岩流冷却后形成的深色细粒岩石；指冷却后的产物。

entries.definition: Any moving mass of material; lava flow narrows it to molten rock and its deposit.
entries.definitionCN: 任何流动的物质团；熔岩流把它收窄到熔融岩石及其堆积物。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Italian dialect source, the real magma boundary and the real compound series.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实存在的意大利方言来源、真实的岩浆分界，以及真实的复合词系列。

normal.en: The dialect word first meant a torrent running down a slope, then settled on the molten stream from a volcano.
normal.cn: 这个方言词本指沿坡冲下的急流，后来固定指火山流出的熔融流体。

normal.en: Underground it is magma, at the surface it is lava: one substance, two stages.
normal.cn: 地下叫岩浆，地表叫熔岩：同一种物质，两个阶段。

normal.en: The compounds line up by shape: lava flow, lava dome, lava tube, pillow lava.
normal.cn: 复合词按形态排开：熔岩流、熔岩穹丘、熔岩管、枕状熔岩。

normal.en: After cooling the material is still called lava, though it has become dark basalt.
normal.cn: 冷却之后，这种材料仍叫熔岩，只是已成了深色玄武岩。

normal.en: The lava lamp is the one everyday use: wax blobs rise and fall as if lava flowed inside the glass.
normal.cn: 熔岩灯是唯一日常可见的用法：蜡块升降，仿佛玻璃里有熔岩在流。

abstract.en: Picture honey falling from a spoon, thickening as it goes, a skin forming first.
abstract.cn: 想象蜂蜜从勺上缓慢垂落，越流越厚，表面先结一层皮。

abstract.en: Picture thick porridge tipped onto a table, still bubbling at the centre while the edge hardens.
abstract.cn: 想象一锅浓粥倒在桌上，中心还在冒泡，边缘已经硬了。

abstract.en: Picture a dark moving line at night whose colour can only be guessed.
abstract.cn: 想象夜里一条移动的暗线，颜色只能靠猜。

examples.en: Lava from the fissure flowed into the valley for three days.
examples.cn: 裂缝中的熔岩流入山谷，持续了三天。

examples.en: The lava had cooled into a dark, glassy crust.
examples.cn: 熔岩冷却成一层深色、带玻璃光泽的硬壳。

examples.en: Tourists queued to watch the wax blobs rise in the lava lamp.
examples.cn: 游客排队观看熔岩灯里蜡块升起。

dict_mnemonic.text: 意大利方言「急流」——从火山口冲出的流动物 → 熔岩

root: 意大利语（那不勒斯方言）lava「急流」进入英语作 lava；更深来源未定，或与拉丁 labes「坠落、滑落」有关（仅属假说），亦有人提出拉丁 lavare「洗」；并非拉丁语直接继承词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow the melt after it escapes: first the substance at the surface, then the stream it forms, the rock it becomes, three shapes cooling gives it, a figurative flood, and finally a cultural object named after the look.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟踪熔体逃出地表之后的经历：先是在地表的物质，然后是它形成的流体、它变成的岩石、冷却赋予它的三种形态、比喻性的涌流，最后是以其外观命名的文化物件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a glowing paste that has escaped its rock lid and now crawls over the ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：一团逃出岩石盖子的灼热糊状物，正在地面上爬行。

branches.en: MATERIAL AND FLOW: the exposed melt and the moving body it makes.
branches.cn: 物质与流动：露出地表的熔体，以及它形成的流动体。

branches.en: COOLED PRODUCT: the melt keeps its name after it hardens into dark rock.
branches.cn: 冷却产物：熔体硬结成深色岩石后仍沿用原名。

branches.en: SHAPES OF FLOW: a dome, a tube and a pillow are three ways the same melt freezes in place.
branches.cn: 流动的形态：穹丘、管道与枕状体，是同一熔体在原地冻住的三种方式。

branches.en: FIGURATIVE FLOOD: heat and unstoppable motion carry over to anything pouring out.
branches.cn: 比喻涌流：高温与不可阻挡的运动被移用到一切大量涌出之物。

branches.en: CULTURAL OBJECT: a lamp borrows the look of rising and sinking melt.
branches.cn: 文化物件：一盏灯借用了熔体升降的外观。

intro.en: Lava has no Latin prefixes or suffixes of its own; it arrived as a whole dialect word, so the items below are compounds and borrowed combining forms rather than true affixes.
intro.cn: lava 没有自己的拉丁前缀或后缀；它作为一个完整的方言词传入，因此下列条目是复合形式与借入的组合成分，而非真正的词缀。

latinIntro.en: No Latin entries are listed: lava is not inherited from Latin, and its possible Latin links are hypotheses rather than a derivational family.
latinIntro.cn: 此处不列拉丁词条：lava 并非由拉丁语继承而来，其可能的拉丁联系只是假说，而非一个派生词族。

items.meaning: torrent; molten rock at the surface
items.example: The word arrived whole, without a Latin prefix.
items.exampleCN: 这个词整体传入，没有拉丁前缀。

items.meaning: noun ending, not a suffix of meaning
items.example: The final -a is an Italian noun ending, not an English suffix.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -a 是意大利语的名词结尾，不是英语后缀。

items.example: The flow reached the road by noon.
items.exampleCN: 熔岩流在正午前抵达公路。

items.example: The dome cracked as it grew.
The tube held a cold river of air.
items.exampleCN: 管道里流着一股冷空气。

items.example: Pillow lava records a submarine eruption.
items.exampleCN: 枕状熔岩记录了水下喷发。

items.example: The lamp was a gift from a friend.

items.exampleCN: 谷底两侧分布着熔岩沉积。

items.structure: Old English molten, past participle of melt
items.exampleCN: 熔化的岩石发出暗红的光。

items.example: Basalt forms most of the ocean floor.
items.exampleCN: 玄武岩构成大部分海底。

definition_zh: 卫生间；厕所；马桶；盥洗间
definition_en: a room with a toilet, the toilet itself, or in older use a place for washing
core_image: 车站尽头一扇小门，门牌上画着一滴水
scene: 火车快到站时，走廊尽头的小门前已经排起了队。He asked the conductor where the lavatory was.
sceneCN: 这里是「卫生间、厕所」（第 1 个义项：带马桶的房间）；句意为他问乘务员洗手间在哪里。可辨识画面：车厢走廊、门前排队的人、门上的小标志。

pos.zh: 卫生间；厕所；马桶；盥洗间

derivatives.zh: 由 lavatory 加 -ial 构成，义为「厕所的」；也指「粗俗下流的」
由拉丁词干 lav-（洗）加 -ation 构成，义为「洗涤」
来自拉丁语 lavabo（我要洗手），义为「洗手盆；洗手礼」

senses.title: A room with a toilet
senses.definition: a room, especially a public one, with a toilet and usually a washbasin
senses.definitionCN: 设有马桶、通常也有洗手盆的房间，尤指公共的
senses.example: The lavatory is at the end of the corridor.
senses.exampleCN: 洗手间在走廊尽头。
senses.why: Latin lavare meant to wash, and a room named after washing kept that name even when the toilet became its main purpose.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 lavare 意为洗，这个以「洗」命名的房间即使马桶成了主要用途，也沿用旧名。

senses.title: The toilet itself
senses.definition: the bowl and seat used as a toilet
senses.definitionCN: 用作马桶的便盆与座圈
senses.example: The lavatory would not flush.
senses.exampleCN: 马桶冲不下去了。
senses.why: Since people name a room by the fixture they go there for, the word for the room shifted onto the bowl inside it.
senses.whyCN: 既然人们用房间里的主要设施来指这个房间，房间的名字就落到了里面的便器上。

senses.title: A place for washing, the older sense
senses.definition: a room or basin used for washing, the original meaning of the word
senses.definitionCN: 用于洗浴或洗手的房间、盆具，是这个词较早的含义
senses.example: The older house had a lavatory off the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 那栋老房子的门厅旁有一间盥洗室。
senses.why: The word began as a washing place, and this sense survives in older buildings and in formal writing.
senses.whyCN: 这个词起初指洗浴之处，这层意思在老式建筑与正式文字里仍然保留。

intro.en: A Latin verb of washing and a Latin place suffix made a word for a washing place, which English later moved to the toilet.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁语「洗」的动词与一个拉丁语地点后缀造出了「洗浴之处」，英语后来把它移到了厕所上。

items.en: Lavare meant to wash, and it is the verb behind the whole family.
items.cn: lavare 意为洗，是这一族词背后的动词。

items.en: Lavatorium named a place for washing, built from the verb and a place suffix.
items.cn: lavatorium 指洗浴之处，由动词加地点后缀构成。

items.en: The word entered church Latin for the basin used in washing rites.
items.cn: 这个词进入教会拉丁语，指行洗礼仪式的盆。

items.en: English lavatory first meant a washing place or a basin, not a toilet.
items.cn: 英语 lavatory 最初指洗浴处或盆具，并非厕所。

items.en: Modern English shifted the word to the room with a toilet, especially in British use.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个词转到带马桶的房间，尤见于英式用法。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words that share the lav- stem or merely the shape; the near-meaning group collects the many polite words for a toilet.
note.cn: 形近组收共用 lav- 词干或只是形状相近的词；近义组收各种对厕所的礼貌说法。

entries.definition: A room for scientific work, close in shape but not in history.
entries.definitionCN: 进行科学工作的房间；形状相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Giving or spending very generously.
entries.definitionCN: 非常大方地给予或花费。

entries.definition: Medical washing out of a body cavity or organ.
entries.definitionCN: 医学上对体腔或器官的冲洗。

entries.definition: Molten rock pouring from a volcano.
entries.definitionCN: 火山喷出的熔岩。

entries.definition: The fixture itself, or the room containing it.
entries.definitionCN: 马桶本身，或装有马桶的房间。

entries.definition: A room for washing, used politely for a toilet in American English.
entries.definitionCN: 洗澡的房间；美式英语中委婉地指厕所。

entries.definition: A room with washing and toilet facilities.
entries.definitionCN: 设有盥洗与如厕设施的房间。

entries.definition: A public toilet, the usual polite word in American English.
entries.definitionCN: 公共厕所，美式英语常用的委婉说法。

normalIntro.en: A verb of washing and a suffix for places explain why this word still sounds like a bathroom in older writing.
normalIntro.cn: 一个「洗」的动词与一个表示地点的后缀，解释了为什么这个词在旧文字里仍像一间盥洗室。

normal.en: Lavare is Latin for to wash, so lavatory begins as a washing place.
normal.cn: lavare 是拉丁语的「洗」，所以 lavatory 原指洗的地方。

normal.en: The ending -torium marks a place, the same shape seen in other Latin place names.
normal.cn: 词尾 -torium 标记地点，在其他拉丁地点名词里也能见到同一形状。

normal.en: Lavatory and lavation share the lav- stem, which is the washing part.
normal.cn: lavatory 与 lavation 共用 lav- 词干，就是「洗」的部分。

normal.en: British English keeps lavatory for a public toilet, while American English prefers restroom.
normal.cn: 英式英语用 lavatory 指公共厕所，美式英语更常用 restroom。

normal.en: Lavatory seat is the part you sit on, a phrase that shows the fixture sense.
normal.cn: lavatory seat 指坐上去的那部分，这个搭配体现了「便器」义。

abstract.en: A room named for washing kept its name when its job changed, a small record of how plumbing moved.
abstract.cn: 一个以「洗」命名的房间在用途改变后仍沿用旧名，这是管道设施变迁的小记录。

abstract.en: The word's politeness comes from distance: it mentions washing instead of what happens there.
abstract.cn: 这个词的委婉来自距离：它提的是洗手，而不是那里真正发生的事。

abstract.en: A Latin place suffix turns an action into a room, so a verb of washing becomes a door you can open.
abstract.cn: 拉丁语的地点后缀把动作变成房间，于是「洗」这个动词成了一扇可以推开的门。

examples.en: The lavatory is at the end of the corridor.
examples.cn: 洗手间在走廊尽头。

examples.en: He asked the conductor where the lavatory was.
examples.cn: 他问乘务员洗手间在哪里。

examples.en: The lavatory would not flush.
examples.cn: 马桶冲不下去了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「拉水」——上完厕所要拉一下水冲干净；记住 lavatory 是厕所。

root: 拉丁语 lavare（洗）加地点后缀 -torium 构成 lavatorium（洗浴之处），后经教会拉丁语进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a place for washing; the senses then move to the room with a toilet, the fixture inside it, and the older washing sense.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是洗浴之处；义项由此转到带马桶的房间、房内的便器，以及较早的洗涤义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small door at the end of a train corridor with a drop of water on its sign.
core.cn: 核心意象：车厢走廊尽头一扇小门，门牌上画着一滴水。

branches.en: a queue outside a door at the end of a carriage
branches.cn: 车厢尽头门前排队的人

branches.en: a handle pulled to flush a bowl
branches.cn: 拉动冲水的把手

branches.en: a basin standing in an old stone washroom
branches.cn: 旧石头盥洗室里的一只盆

branches.en: a sign showing a drop of water on a door
branches.cn: 门上画着一滴水的标志

branches.en: a row of washing bowls in a church
branches.cn: 教堂里一排用于洗礼仪式的盆

intro.en: A Latin verb of washing, a Latin place suffix and one English adjective ending build this word.
intro.cn: 一个表示洗的拉丁动词、一个拉丁地点后缀与一个英语形容词词尾构成了这个词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaning: room for washing, then a toilet
I shall wash, a washing basin

definition_zh: 草坪；草地
definition_en: an area of short cut grass, especially around a house
core_image: 一片修剪整齐的绿草，边缘还留着割草机压出的条纹
scene: 清晨的院子里，草叶上还挂着露水。He spent the morning mowing the lawn.
sceneCN: 这里是「草坪」（第 1 个义项：修剪过的草地）；句意为他花了一上午修剪草坪。图中可辨识物件：带露水的草叶、割草机、院墙。

derivatives.zh: 由 lawn 与 mower 复合，义为「割草机」
由 lawn 加 -y 构成，义为「像草坪的；多草的」

senses.title: An area of cut grass
senses.definition: a piece of ground covered with short, regularly cut grass, especially near a house
senses.definitionCN: 一块覆盖着修剪整齐的短草的地面，尤指房屋附近
senses.example: He spent the morning mowing the lawn.
senses.exampleCN: 他花了一上午修剪草坪。
senses.why: Lawn began as a word for a clearing or open glade; once people kept such grass short, the word moved to the mown ground itself.
senses.whyCN: lawn 最初指林中空地，后来人们把这种草地保持得很短，词义就转到修剪过的草地本身。

senses.title: A fine linen fabric
senses.definition: a fine, light linen cloth used for shirts and handkerchiefs
senses.definitionCN: 一种精细轻薄的亚麻布，用于衬衫和手帕
senses.example: The collar was made of crisp white lawn.
senses.exampleCN: 衣领是用挺括的白色细麻布做的。
senses.why: This sense comes from a different place name and a different history; it is a look-alike that English spelled the same way.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项来自另一个地名和另一段历史，是英语中拼写碰巧相同的同形词。

intro.en: Lawn meaning grass comes from a word for a clearing; lawn meaning fine linen comes separately from the French town of Laon.
intro.cn: 表示「草坪」的 lawn 来自「林中空地」一词；表示「细麻布」的 lawn 则另来自法国城市拉昂。

items.en: Lande meant a heath, moor or open clearing, a piece of land without trees.
items.cn: lande 意为荒地、荒原或林间空地，指没有树木的一片地。

items.en: The French word is often traced to a Gaulish root for heath or open ground, but the evidence is not conclusive.
items.cn: 这个法语词常被追溯到高卢语中表示荒地或空地的词根，但证据并不充分。

items.en: Middle English launde names a glade or open grassy space.
items.cn: 中古英语 launde 指林间空地或多草的开放空间。

items.en: By the sixteenth century the sense narrows to ground kept short by mowing.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，词义收窄为靠修剪保持短草的草地。

items.en: Modern English lawn means the garden grass, while the linen sense survives separately from Laon.
items.cn: 现代英语 lawn 指庭院草坪，而细麻布义则另从拉昂的地名独立留存。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words formed from lawn and its history; the near-meaning group gathers ground covered with grass.
note.cn: 形近组收由 lawn 及其历史形成的词；近义组收覆盖草的地面。

entries.definition: A machine used to cut grass.
entries.definitionCN: 割草机。

entries.definition: A light chair for sitting outdoors.
entries.definitionCN: 草坪椅。

entries.definition: A Middle English word for a glade or open ground.
entries.definitionCN: 中古英语中表示林间空地的词。

entries.definition: The green plants that cover the ground.
entries.definitionCN: 草；草地。

entries.definition: Short grass and the soil under it.
entries.definitionCN: 草皮。

entries.definition: A piece of grassy ground, especially in a village.
entries.definitionCN: 绿地；村中草地。

entries.definition: A field of grass and flowers.
entries.definitionCN: 草地；牧场。

normalIntro.en: The garden word and the linen word are two histories that happen to share a spelling.
normalIntro.cn: 草坪词与麻布词是两段恰好共享拼写的历史。

normal.en: Lawn for grass is related to land and glade, not to the linen.
normal.cn: 表示草坪的 lawn 与 land、glade 有关，与麻布无关。

normal.en: Mow the lawn is the fixed phrase for cutting it.
normal.cn: mow the lawn 是「修剪草坪」的固定搭配。

normal.en: Lawnmower joins lawn and mower in one word.
normal.cn: lawnmower 把 lawn 与 mower 合成一个词。

normal.en: The linen lawn is named after Laon in France.
normal.cn: 细麻布 lawn 得名于法国城市拉昂。

normal.en: Lawns takes -s in the plural: two lawns, front and back.
normal.cn: 复数加 -s：two lawns，前后两块草坪。

abstract.en: A word for wild clearing became a word for a carefully kept square of grass.
abstract.cn: 一个表示荒野空地的词，变成了精心维护的一方草地。

abstract.en: Two unrelated histories can hide behind one spelling, and only context separates them.
abstract.cn: 两段无关的历史可以藏在同一个拼写后面，只有上下文能把它们分开。

abstract.en: A lawn is nature kept at a chosen length, a small argument between growth and the mower.
abstract.cn: 草坪是被维持在选定长度的自然，是生长与割草机之间的一场小争论。

examples.en: He spent the morning mowing the lawn.
examples.cn: 他花了一上午修剪草坪。

examples.en: The children ran across the front lawn.
examples.cn: 孩子们跑过前院草坪。

examples.en: The collar was made of crisp white lawn.
examples.cn: 衣领是用挺括的白色细麻布做的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「隆」——草地长得隆隆一片，就是 lawn。

root: 表示草坪义来自古法语 lande（荒地、空地），更早一般追溯到高卢语；细麻布义另来自法国地名 Laon。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a kept-short grassy ground; a second, unrelated sense names a fine linen.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是维护得很短的草地；另一个无关义项指一种细麻布。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a square of green grass with mower stripes still visible along its edge.
core.cn: 核心意象：一方绿草，边缘还留着割草机的条纹。

branches.en: a striped lawn seen from a kitchen window
branches.cn: 从厨房窗里看见的条纹草坪

branches.en: a mower turning at the edge of the grass
branches.cn: 在草地边缘转弯的割草机

branches.en: a white collar folded on a shirt
branches.cn: 衬衫上折好的白领

branches.en: a handkerchief thin enough to see light through
branches.cn: 薄得透光的手帕

branches.en: one spelling, two unrelated histories
branches.cn: 一个拼写，两段无关的历史

intro.en: The grass word is a French-derived stem; its family grows by compounding, and the linen word is a separate place name.

senses.title: A civil case in court
senses.titleCN: 已进入法院的民事案件
senses.definition: a dispute between private parties that has been brought before a court
senses.definitionCN: 私人之间已提交法院审理的争议
senses.example: The neighbor filed a lawsuit over the boundary wall.
senses.exampleCN: 邻居就那道界墙提起了诉讼。
senses.why: Law fixes the rule and suit is the following of a case through court, so the compound names a dispute that has been converted into a numbered proceeding.
senses.whyCN: law 定下规则，suit 指按规则一路跟下去，于是这个词指的是一场争执被转成有编号的程序。

senses.title: The act of suing
senses.definition: the step of starting legal proceedings against someone
senses.definitionCN: 对某人启动法律程序的那一步
senses.example: Filing the lawsuit took longer than the hearing itself.
senses.exampleCN: 提起诉讼花的时间比开庭本身还长。
senses.why: The word names the thing filed as well as the filing, because in law the paper and the act that delivers it are hard to separate.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既指被递交的那份东西，也指递交这个动作，因为在法律上文书与递交行为很难分开。

senses.title: A claim for money
senses.definition: a suit asking the court to order payment or compensation
senses.definitionCN: 请求法院判令付款或赔偿的诉讼
senses.example: The builder brought a lawsuit for the final payment.
senses.exampleCN: 施工方为尾款提起了一桩诉讼。
senses.why: Most civil suits end in a money figure, so the word often means a demand for damages rather than a demand for an order.
senses.whyCN: 多数民事案件最后都落到一个金额上，所以这个词常指索赔，而不是请求作出某种命令。

senses.title: A suit over reputation
senses.definition: a suit claiming harm to reputation or to a published name
senses.definitionCN: 主张名誉或姓名被损害的诉讼
senses.example: The actor's lawsuit alleged that the article had ruined his name.
senses.exampleCN: 这名演员的诉讼称那篇文章毁了他的名声。
senses.why: Harm that leaves no visible mark still needs a form, and a lawsuit supplies the form: the injury is written down and priced.
senses.whyCN: 看不见的伤害也需要一个形式，诉讼正好提供这个形式：把损害写下来并标出价码。

senses.title: A business dispute taken to court
senses.definition: a suit between companies over contracts, supply or competition
senses.definitionCN: 公司之间因合同、供货或竞争而起的诉讼
senses.example: The two airlines spent four years in a lawsuit over landing slots.
senses.exampleCN: 两家航空公司为起降时段打了四年官司。
senses.why: Where contracts are long and money is large, the threat of a lawsuit becomes a normal instrument of business planning.
senses.whyCN: 合同长、金额大的地方，诉讼威胁就成了商业筹划中的常规工具。

senses.title: A suit brought by many
senses.titleCN: 由许多人共同提起的诉讼
senses.definition: a suit in which a group of people with the same injury sue together
senses.definitionCN: 一群受同一损害的人共同提起的诉讼
senses.example: Thousands of customers joined the lawsuit against the maker.
senses.exampleCN: 数千名顾客加入了针对制造商的那桩诉讼。
senses.why: One small claim is expensive to pursue; joining many small claims into one lawsuit makes the cost bearable, so the word covers group actions.
senses.whyCN: 单笔小额索赔诉讼成本太高，把许多小额请求并成一案才划得来，于是这个词也覆盖群体索赔。

senses.title: A suit as leverage
senses.titleCN: 作为谈判筹码的诉讼威胁
senses.definition: the mention of a possible suit used to pressure a settlement
senses.definitionCN: 以可能打官司来施压、促成和解的用法
senses.example: A quiet mention of a lawsuit was enough to bring them back to the table.
senses.exampleCN: 一句轻描淡写的诉讼威胁就足以把他们拉回谈判桌。
senses.why: Because filing is cheap and public, the word can be used before any paper exists, as a warning rather than a description.
senses.whyCN: 因为立案便宜又公开，这个词可以在任何文书存在之前就使用，作为警告而不是描述。

senses.title: The long life of a case
senses.definition: the whole course of a case, from filing through appeal
senses.definitionCN: 从立案到上诉的整个案件过程
senses.example: The lawsuit outlasted two of the lawyers who started it.
senses.exampleCN: 这桩官司比最初接手的两名律师撑得还久。
senses.why: Since a contested case can run for years, the same noun can name not the paper but the entire stretch of time it keeps alive.
senses.whyCN: 有争议的案件能拖很多年，于是同一个名词也可以不指那份文书，而指它维持的整段时间。

intro.en: Lawsuit joins two old English nouns of different ancestry: law from Old Norse, suit from Latin by way of French. The compound itself is early modern.
intro.cn: lawsuit 把两个来源不同的古老英语名词接在一起：law 来自古诺斯语，suit 经法语来自拉丁语。复合词本身出现于近代早期。

items.en: Old Norse lag meant 'something laid down, a layer', and it gave Old English lagu 'law, rule'. The same Germanic root lies behind lay, and the legal sense is 'that which is laid down' for people to follow.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 lag 意为「被放下之物、一层」，由此产生古英语 lagu「法律、规则」。同一日耳曼词根也在 lay 之中，法律义就是「为众人放下、须遵守的东西」。

items.en: Sequi meant 'to follow'. Its past participle secutus and the derived noun *sequita underlie a whole family of following words, including sequence, consequent and suit.
items.cn: sequi 意为「跟随」。其过去分词 secutus 与派生名词 *sequita 支撑了一整族表示「跟随」的词，包括 sequence、consequent 与 suit。

items.en: Old French suite meant a following, a train of attendants, or a set of things in order; English borrowed it in the thirteenth century as suit.
items.cn: 古法语 suite 指跟随、随从队伍或一组有序之物；英语在十三世纪借入，写作 suit。

items.en: By the fourteenth century English suit at law meant the pursuit of a case in court, and the verb sue was formed from it. This is the sense that survives inside lawsuit.
items.cn: 到十四世纪，英语里「依法律追究」的说法已指在法院追究一桩案件，动词「起诉」也由此产生。lawsuit 里保留的正是这一义。

items.en: Lawsuit appears in the seventeenth century, joining law to suit so that the legal reading would be unmistakable; earlier writers said suit or action.
items.cn: lawsuit 于十七世纪出现，把「法律」接到「追究」上，使法律义不再有歧义；更早的作者只说「诉」或「诉讼」。

items.en: The first date usually given for the compound is an approximation drawn from printed citations, and dictionaries differ by a few decades; the sources of both halves are not in doubt.
items.cn: 这个复合词通常给出的首见年代，是从印刷书证推算的约数，各家辞书相差数十年；两半的来源本身并无疑问。

note.en: Group one holds words of the same suit family, including one near homophone; group two holds the everyday names for legal proceedings.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 suit 词族的词，其中一个读音极近；第二组是法律程序的日常说法。

entries.definition: The root noun: legal action in older use, and also a set of clothes or a set of cards.
entries.definitionCN: 词根名词：旧用法指诉讼，也指一套衣服或一组同花色的牌。

entries.definition: A set of rooms or a set of musical pieces; it came from the same French word but never took the legal sense.
entries.definitionCN: 一套房间或一组乐曲；来自同一个法语词，却从未发展出法律义。

entries.definition: The verb formed from suit: to bring a case against someone.
entries.definitionCN: 由 suit 形成的动词：对某人提起诉讼。

entries.definition: The rule system itself, not the case; law is Germanic while suit is Latin in origin.
entries.definitionCN: 规则体系本身，不是案件；law 是日耳曼来源，suit 才是拉丁来源。

entries.definition: To plunge into liquid or to pickle; the vowel and the final consonant are close, but the word is unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 浸入液体或腌渍；元音与词尾相近，但这个词毫无亲缘关系。

entries.definition: The general word for a matter before a court; it can be civil or criminal.
entries.definitionCN: 法院受理事项的通称，民事刑事皆可。

entries.definition: The formal British term for civil proceedings, as in bring an action.
entries.definitionCN: 英式正式用语，指民事诉讼程序。

entries.definition: Litigation names the activity or the whole set of proceedings, not one countable case.
entries.definitionCN: 指诉讼活动或一整批程序，不指单件可数的案件。

entries.definition: The demand stated inside a lawsuit; a claim may exist before any suit is filed.
entries.definitionCN: 诉讼中提出的请求；请求可以在立案之前就存在。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the two real halves, the real verb formed from suit, and the real phrases used in practice.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用两个真实成分、由 suit 形成的真实动词，以及实务中真实的固定说法。

normal.en: Law plus suit: the rule plus the following of a case under it.
normal.cn: law 加 suit：规则，加上按规则一路追究一桩案子。

normal.en: Suit, sue and suite share one Latin verb of following; only suit and sue took the legal path.
normal.cn: suit、sue 与 suite 共享同一个表示「跟随」的拉丁动词，只有前两个走了法律这条路。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the stages: file a lawsuit, settle a lawsuit, face a lawsuit.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出阶段：提起诉讼、和解结案、面临诉讼。

normal.en: A class-action lawsuit is one suit carrying many claims, which is why one word covers a crowd.
normal.cn: 集体诉讼是一案承载许多请求，所以一个词就能覆盖一群人。

normal.en: Law itself came from Old Norse, not from Latin, so the two halves of this compound are strangers joined late.
normal.cn: law 本身来自古诺斯语而非拉丁语，所以这个复合词的两半是晚年才结亲的陌生人。

abstract.en: Picture a quarrel being folded into a paper folder and given a number: the moment it gets a number, it becomes a lawsuit.
abstract.cn: 想象一场口角被折进一个纸夹并编上号：它一拿到编号，就成了 lawsuit。

abstract.en: Picture two people walking the same corridor for years, always one behind the other: that is what following a case means.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人多年走在同一条走廊上，永远一个跟着另一个：这就是「追究一桩案子」的样子。

abstract.en: Picture a small stone placed on a scale: the scale is the law, the stone is the claim, and the lawsuit is the act of putting it there.
abstract.cn: 想象一块小石头被放上天平：天平是法律，石头是请求，而 lawsuit 就是把它放上去的那个动作。

examples.en: The city settled the lawsuit before the trial date was set.
examples.cn: 市里在确定开庭日期之前就和解了这桩诉讼。

examples.en: A single lawsuit can force a manufacturer to redesign a product.
examples.cn: 一桩诉讼就能迫使制造商重新设计产品。

examples.en: She kept every receipt in case of a future lawsuit.
examples.cn: 她留好每一张收据，以防日后打官司。

dict_mnemonic.text: law（法律）+ suit（跟随、追究）——按法律一路追究下去的那件事 → 诉讼、官司

root: law 来自古诺斯语 lag（被放下之物），经古英语 lagu 成为「法律」；suit 经古法语 suite 上溯拉丁 sequi（跟随）。lawsuit 为十七世纪英语复合词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow a case from being filed, through the claim it states and the parties who bring it, to the years it can run and the pressure its mere mention creates.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项跟着一桩案件走：从立案，到它写明的请求、提起诉讼的人，再到它可能拖的年份，最后到仅凭提及就能产生的压力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a quarrel folded into a numbered file and carried down a long corridor.
core.cn: 核心意象：一场争执被折进一份编号案卷，沿着长走廊被一路带下去。

branches.en: THE FILE ITSELF: the dispute has become an object with a number, and that object is the lawsuit.
branches.cn: 案卷本身：争执变成一个带编号的东西，这个东西就是诉讼。

branches.en: THE OPENING ACT: the filing is the moment the file begins, so the word also names the doing.
branches.cn: 开启动作：立案是案卷开始的那一刻，所以这个词也指那个动作。

branches.en: WHAT IS ASKED FOR: money or reputation, both get written into the claim.
branches.cn: 请求什么：钱或名誉，都被写进请求里。

branches.en: WHO CARRIES IT: one company or a crowd of customers can be the party that sets the file moving.
branches.cn: 谁在推动：一家公司或一大群顾客都可能成为让案卷往前走的一方。

branches.en: THE FILE AS FORCE: before it exists it can still pressure, and once it exists it can outlast the people who opened it.
branches.cn: 案卷的力量：存在之前就能施压，存在之后又能比立案的人活得更久。

intro.en: Lawsuit is a compound of two free nouns, so its structure is read by joining rather than by adding affixes; only the derived verb and adjective show suffixes.
intro.cn: lawsuit 由两个自由名词复合而成，结构靠拼接来读，而不是靠加词缀；只有派生出的动词与形容词带后缀。

latinIntro.en: Suit goes back to Latin sequi 'to follow', while law is Germanic and unrelated to Latin lex 'law'. The family of sequi also gives sequence, consequent and obsequious.
latinIntro.cn: suit 上溯拉丁 sequi「跟随」；law 是日耳曼语词，与拉丁 lex「法律」并无亲缘。sequi 词族还衍生 sequence、consequent 与 obsequious。

items.structure: law (free noun from Old English lagu, from Old Norse lag)
items.meaning: a rule laid down for a community
items.meaningCN: 为群体放下、须遵守的规则
items.example: The new law takes effect in spring.

items.structure: suit (free noun from Old French suite, from Latin sequi)
items.example: He brought a suit against the firm.
items.exampleCN: 他对这家公司提起了诉讼。

items.structure: law + suit (compound of two free nouns)
items.meaning: a civil case brought under the law
items.meaningCN: 依法律提起的民事案件（复合后由「跟随」收窄为「进入法院的案件」）

items.meaning: to bring a case against someone
items.meaningCN: 对某人提起诉讼（由名词逆构出动词，语义由「跟随」变为「启动追究」）

items.meaning: the act of bringing a case
items.meaningCN: 提起诉讼的行为（动名词后缀把动作名词化）
items.example: Suing is cheaper than most people think.
items.exampleCN: 打官司比多数人想的便宜。

items.meaningCN: 法律允许的（形容词后缀把规则变成性质）
无法无天的（否定后缀把「有规则」翻成「无规则」）
items.example: The district grew lawless after the floods.
items.exampleCN: 洪水之后该地区变得无法无天。

items.structure: law + -yer (person suffix, variant of Old French -ier)
items.meaningCN: 以法律为业的人（人名词缀把规则变成一个职业者）

items.structure: suit + case (compound, different sense of suit)
items.meaningCN: 装衣物的旅行箱（这里的 suit 取「一套衣服」义，与诉讼义无关）

core_image: 一摞贴着彩色标签的卷宗堆在办公桌上，桌边的人正把其中一条条款圈出来给来访者看

senses.title: A person who practises law
senses.definition: someone whose profession is law, whether advising or representing
senses.definitionCN: 以法律为职业的人，提供咨询或代理皆可
senses.example: The lawyer marked three clauses that could cost the tenant money.
senses.exampleCN: 律师标出了三条可能让租客多花钱的条款。
senses.why: The word is built from law plus an agent ending, so it names the profession by its subject matter rather than by a court role.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由「法律」加施事后缀构成，所以它按业务内容命名职业，而不是按法庭角色命名。

senses.title: An adviser working outside court
senses.definition: a legal adviser whose work is done in an office rather than in court
senses.definitionCN: 主要在办公室而非法庭上工作的法律顾问
senses.example: Our lawyer reviewed the insurance policy line by line.
senses.exampleCN: 我们的律师逐行审阅了保险条款。
senses.why: Most legal work is paperwork and advice, so the everyday word usually points to the desk rather than to the dock.
senses.whyCN: 多数法律工作是文书与咨询，所以这个日常词通常指向办公桌，而不是法庭上的席位。

senses.title: An advocate who speaks in court
senses.definition: a legal practitioner who argues a case before a judge
senses.definitionCN: 在法官面前为案件辩论的执业者
senses.example: The lawyer spoke for forty minutes without looking at her notes.
senses.exampleCN: 这位律师讲了四十分钟，全程没看笔记。
senses.why: The same noun serves the courtroom because advocacy is the part of the profession the public sees and remembers.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词也用于法庭，因为辩护是公众看得见、记得住的那部分工作。

senses.title: The profession as a group
senses.definition: lawyers considered collectively, often in commentary or criticism
senses.definitionCN: 被整体看待的律师，常用于评论或批评
senses.example: The lawyers for both sides met privately before the hearing.
senses.exampleCN: 开庭前，双方的律师私下见了面。
senses.why: A countable noun used in the plural can stand for a whole trade, which is why the word appears in sentences about the profession as a force.
senses.whyCN: 可数名词用复数时可以代表整个行业，所以这个词会出现在把律师界当作一股力量的句子里。

senses.title: A specialist in one branch
senses.definition: a practitioner who works in a particular field of law
senses.definitionCN: 在某一法律领域执业的律师
senses.example: They consulted a patent lawyer before filing the design.
senses.exampleCN: 申请外观设计前，他们咨询了专利律师。
senses.why: Modern law divides into fields, and the word attaches to the field as a modifier, turning the general noun into a specialism.
senses.whyCN: 现代法律分成许多领域，这个词作为修饰成分附着在领域上，就把通称变成了专业分工。

senses.title: The person who drafts the papers
senses.definition: the practitioner who prepares contracts, deeds and other documents
senses.definitionCN: 准备合同、契据等文书的执业者
senses.example: The lawyer drafted the deed so that either heir could sell.
senses.exampleCN: 律师起草的契据让两位继承人都能出售。
senses.why: Drafting is invisible in court but decisive in outcome, so the word also covers the quiet work behind a signature.
senses.whyCN: 起草在法庭上看不见，却决定结果，所以这个词也覆盖签名背后那份安静的工作。

senses.title: A sea lawyer
senses.titleCN: 好抬杠的水手；爱抠规则的人
senses.definition: an argumentative sailor, or anyone who quibbles about rules without authority
senses.definitionCN: 爱争辩的水手，或任何没有职权却抠规则字眼的人
senses.example: The cook was a sea lawyer who could quote every regulation but never follow one.
senses.exampleCN: 那个厨子是个爱抬杠的水手，条条规则都能背，却一条也不照做。
senses.why: Sailors with time on their hands argued about regulations, and the fixed phrase transferred that habit to land as a mild insult.
senses.whyCN: 水手闲来无事就争论规章，这个固定说法把这种习气带上岸，成了轻度的讥称。

senses.title: A clever arguer on technicalities
senses.definition: a person who argues by exploiting fine points rather than by merit
senses.definitionCN: 靠抠细枝末节而非讲道理取胜的人
senses.example: You do not need to be a lawyer to win that argument, only patient.
senses.exampleCN: 赢那场争论不必是律师，只需要有耐心。
senses.why: Because the trade is associated with precise wording, the noun can describe anyone who fights with clauses instead of facts.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个行业与精确措辞联系在一起，这个名词便能描述任何用条款而非事实来争论的人。

intro.en: Lawyer is an English compound of law and an agent ending. Law comes from Old Norse lag 'something laid down', while the ending is a variant of -ier from Old French, ultimately Latin -arius.
intro.cn: lawyer 是英语用 law 加施事后缀构成的复合词。law 来自古诺斯语 lag「被放下的东西」，词尾则是古法语 -ier 的变体，最终上溯拉丁 -arius。

items.en: Lag meant something laid down, a layer or a fixed order; its plural log named customary law in the Norse-speaking world.
items.cn: lag 意为被放下的东西、一层或既定秩序；其复数 lǫg 在诺斯语世界指习惯法。

items.en: English borrowed lagu for law, covering both the body of rules and the custom of a district, a word that displaced the older native term.
items.cn: 英语借入 lagu 表示法律，既指整套规则，也指一地的习惯，并取代了更早的本族词。

items.en: The Latin agent suffix -arius, through Old French -ier, formed words for people concerned with a thing, and it is the source of the ending here.
items.cn: 拉丁施事后缀 -arius 经古法语 -ier，构成「与某物打交道的人」，这里这个词尾正源于此。

items.en: Middle English had lawier beside lawyer; the spelling with y won out, and the word settled on the profession as a whole.
items.cn: 中古英语里 lawier 与 lawyer 并存，带 y 的拼法最终胜出，这个词也固定指整个职业。

items.en: Modern English uses lawyer as the neutral everyday term, while attorney carries American formality and counsel carries courtroom colour.
items.cn: 现代英语把 lawyer 当作中性日常说法，attorney 带美国式的正式感，counsel 则带法庭色彩。

note.en: Group one separates the base word and the derived family from two look-alikes with other origins; group two sets the plain word against the formal and regional titles.
note.cn: 第一组把基础词与派生词族，同两个来源不同的形近词分开；第二组把日常通称与正式称谓、地区称谓作对照。

entries.definition: The rules themselves; lawyer is the person whose trade is those rules.
entries.definitionCN: 指规则本身；lawyer 是以这些规则为业的人。

entries.definition: Resembling a lawyer or the manner of legal argument, not a person.
entries.definitionCN: 像律师的、像法律辩论腔调的，不是指人。

entries.definition: The practice or craft of being a lawyer, viewed as work rather than as a role.
entries.definitionCN: 指律师的实务与手艺，看作工作而非角色。

entries.definition: One who saws wood, from saw plus the same agent ending; the shape matches but the base is a tool, not law.
entries.definitionCN: 锯木的人，由 saw 加同一个施事后缀构成；外形相似，基础词却是工具而非法律。

entries.definition: A law-enforcement officer, built from law plus man; it names an officer, not a legal adviser.
entries.definitionCN: 执法官员，由 law 加 man 构成；它指警官，不是法律顾问。

entries.definition: The formal American word for a legal representative, also used in official titles.
entries.definitionCN: 美国指法律代理人的正式说法，也用于官方头衔。

entries.definition: A legal adviser or the advocates in a case, often a mass noun with a formal tone.
entries.definitionCN: 法律顾问或案中的辩护人，常作不可数名词，语气正式。

entries.definition: In Britain, the lawyer who advises and prepares documents rather than pleading in higher courts.
entries.definitionCN: 在英国，指提供咨询、准备文书而不在高等法院辩论的律师。

entries.definition: In Britain, a lawyer specially qualified to plead in the higher courts.
entries.definitionCN: 在英国，指有资格在高等法院出庭辩论的律师。

entries.definition: A person who pleads for another, in law or in a cause; the word stresses speaking for someone.
entries.definitionCN: 为他人或某项事业辩护的人；这个词强调替人发声。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Norse source of law and the real agent ending.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用 law 真实的诺斯语来源，以及真实的施事后缀。

normal.en: Law is 'what is laid down', and a lawyer is the person who works with what is laid down.
normal.cn: law 是「被放下的东西」，lawyer 就是与这些既定规则打交道的人。

normal.en: The -yer ending is a spelling of the agent ending that also built sawyer, a woodcutter.
normal.cn: -yer 是施事后缀的一种拼法，它也构成了 sawyer，即锯木人。

normal.en: Sawyer looks like lawyer but starts from a tool, so the two words share an ending and nothing else.
normal.cn: sawyer 形似 lawyer，却从工具起头，两词只共享词尾，别无其他。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the settings: a practising lawyer, a defence lawyer, a company lawyer.
normal.cn: 固定说法标出场景：执业律师、辩护律师、公司法务。

normal.en: The plain word sits between attorney and counsel: less formal than one, less courtroom-bound than the other.
normal.cn: 这个通称夹在 attorney 与 counsel 之间：比前者随意，比后者少些法庭气。

abstract.en: Picture a stack of folders with coloured tabs, one tab for each field of law.
abstract.cn: 想象一摞贴着彩色标签的卷宗，每个法律领域一个标签。

abstract.en: Picture a person reading a contract with a red pen, circling what could cost money.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人拿着红笔读合同，圈出可能花钱的地方。

abstract.en: Picture a trade that exists because rules are written down and someone must read them closely.
abstract.cn: 想象一门行业的存在理由：规则被写下来，总得有人仔细去读。

examples.en: A good lawyer tells you what not to sign, not only what to sign.
examples.cn: 好律师会告诉你什么别签，而不只是什么该签。

examples.en: The company keeps two lawyers in house and hires outside counsel for big cases.
examples.cn: 公司内部留了两名律师，大案子再请外部顾问。

examples.en: He joked that every family needs a doctor, a lawyer and a locksmith.
examples.cn: 他开玩笑说，每个家庭都需要一个医生、一个律师和一个锁匠。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「老爷」——旧时替人写状纸、讲规矩的师爷，如今叫 lawyer → 律师

root: 英语 law（法律，源自古诺斯语 lag「被放下之物」）加施事后缀 -yer（古法语 -ier 的变体，上溯拉丁 -arius）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from the profession as a whole, through office advice, courtroom advocacy, the trade seen as a group, specialist practice and document drafting, to the sea lawyer and the mere quibbler.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从整个职业开始，经办公室咨询、出庭辩护、作为群体的律师界、专长执业与文书起草，最后到「好抬杠的水手」和只会钻字眼的争辩者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of tabbed files on a desk, one clause circled in red.
core.cn: 核心意象：办公桌上一摞贴标签的卷宗，其中一条被红笔圈出。

branches.en: THE TRADE: the agent ending turns the rules into a person whose work they are.
branches.cn: 职业：施事后缀把「规则」变成以此为业的人。

branches.en: THE DESK: most of the work is reading, warning and drafting outside court.
branches.cn: 办公桌：多数工作是在法庭之外阅读、提醒与起草。

branches.en: THE VOICE AND THE BODY: the same noun covers the speaker in court and the profession as a collective force.
branches.cn: 声音与群体：同一个名词既指庭上发言者，也指作为一股力量的整个行业。

branches.en: THE NARROWING: fields and paperwork split the general word into specialisms and quiet desk work.
branches.cn: 细分：领域与文书把这个通称分成专业分工与安静的案头工作。

branches.en: THE INSULT: the trade's prestige also produces mock titles for quibblers and technical arguers.
branches.cn: 讥称：这个行业的声望也造出了挖苦人的称号，指爱抬杠与钻字眼的人。

intro.en: Lawyer is a home-built English compound: a Norse-derived noun plus a French-derived agent ending.
intro.cn: lawyer 是英语本土拼装的复合词：一个源自诺斯语的名词，加一个源自法语的施事后缀。

latinIntro.en: The ending is Latin -arius, which reached English through Old French -ier; the noun law itself is not Latin but Norse.
latinIntro.cn: 词尾是拉丁 -arius，经古法语 -ier 进入英语；而名词 law 本身并非拉丁语，而是诺斯语。

items.example: The Norse noun named what was laid down.
items.exampleCN: 这个诺斯语名词命名被放下的东西。

items.example: Lagu covered both statute and custom.
items.exampleCN: lagu 既指成文规则，也指习惯。

items.meaningCN: 与……打交道的人（施事后缀）
items.example: The suffix built words for trades.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成表示行业的词。

items.meaningCN: 从事……的人（经法语转写的施事词尾）
items.example: French kept the Latin suffix in a shorter form.
items.exampleCN: 法语把这个拉丁后缀保留成更短的形式。

items.meaningCN: 施事词尾（英语中的另一种拼法）
items.example: Lawyer and sawyer share this spelling.
items.exampleCN: lawyer 与 sawyer 共享这一拼法。

items.meaningCN: 以法律为业的人（基础词加施事后缀，指职业而非一次动作）
items.exampleCN: 一位律师读了这份租约。

items.meaning: in the manner of a lawyer
items.meaningCN: 像律师的（形容词后缀把职业转成风格）
items.example: He answered in a lawyerly way.
items.exampleCN: 他用律师式的措辞回答。

items.meaningCN: 律师实务（动名词后缀把角色转成活动）
items.exampleCN: 扎实的律师实务避免了损失。

律师实务

definition_zh: 层；层次；地层；涂层；产蛋鸡
definition_en: a thickness or sheet of material covering a surface; one of several levels in a system; a hen that lays eggs
core_image: 一张一张薄片叠起来，像千层饼的横截面，每一层都清晰可数
scene: 地质课上，老师用铲子切开岩壁，露出水平排列的一层层岩石。他指着说：Each layer was laid down in a different age.
sceneCN: 这里 layer 是「岩层、地层」（第 3 个义项：地质沉积层）；句意：每一层岩石都是在不同年代沉积下来的。图中可辨识物件：岩壁、铲子、水平岩层、地质锤。

derivatives.zh: 分层的；有层次的
分层；层叠；压条繁殖
多层的；多层结构

senses.title: A sheet laid over a surface
senses.titleCN: 铺在表面上的一层：涂层、薄层
senses.definition: a thickness or sheet of material that covers a surface
senses.definitionCN: 覆盖在表面上的一层材料或一片物质
senses.example: A thin layer of dust covered the table.
senses.exampleCN: 桌上覆盖着一层薄薄的灰。
senses.why: Layer is lay + -er: 'that which is laid'. A layer is material placed down on a surface, seen as one sheet rather than as a mass.
senses.whyCN: layer 是 lay 加 -er，即“被铺下的东西”。一层就是把材料铺在表面上，被看作一片，而不是一团。

senses.title: One level in a stack of levels
senses.titleCN: 层层结构中的一级：层次
senses.definition: one of several levels in a system, idea or organization, each built on or above another
senses.definitionCN: 系统、思想或组织中的若干层级之一，每一层建立在另一层之上
senses.example: The novel works on several layers of meaning.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说在好几层意义上成立。
senses.why: Anything that can be laid down one piece over another can be imagined as a stack. Ideas and organizations borrow the physical stack and call each level a layer.
senses.whyCN: 任何能一层压一层铺放的东西，都可以被想象成一摞。思想与组织借用这个物理堆叠，把每一级称为一层。

senses.title: A stratum in the earth
senses.definition: in geology, a band of rock or soil of one kind, deposited at a particular period
senses.definitionCN: 地质学中，某一时期沉积形成的同一种岩石或土壤带
senses.example: The fossils were found in a layer of limestone.
senses.exampleCN: 化石是在一层石灰岩中发现的。
senses.why: Sediment settles in sheets, one age on top of another. Geology sees the earth's history as a stack of layers, so the word becomes a technical term for a stratum.
senses.whyCN: 沉积物一片一片落下，一个年代压在另一个年代上。地质学把地球历史看成一摞层，于是这个词成为“地层”的术语。

senses.title: A band around the planet
senses.titleCN: 包围地球的一带：大气层
senses.definition: in geography, a distinct band of the atmosphere or ocean at a particular height or depth
senses.definitionCN: 地理学中，大气或海洋在特定高度或深度上的一条明显带
senses.example: The ozone layer protects us from harmful radiation.
senses.exampleCN: 臭氧层保护我们免受有害辐射。
senses.why: The atmosphere is arranged in shells, one above another. Each shell is a layer because it can be drawn as a band laid over the one below.
senses.whyCN: 大气按壳层排列，一层在另一层之上。每个壳层都是一层，因为它可以被画成覆盖在下面那层上的一条带。

senses.title: A level in software
senses.titleCN: 软件中的一层：分层架构
senses.definition: in computing, one level of a system or protocol that communicates with the levels above and below it
senses.definitionCN: 计算机中，与上下层通信的系统或协议的一级
senses.example: The application layer sits above the network layer.
senses.exampleCN: 应用层位于网络层之上。
senses.why: Software designers picture a system as a stack of levels, each hiding the details of the one below. The physical stack of sheets becomes an architecture.
senses.whyCN: 软件设计者把系统想象成一摞层级，每一层隐藏下面一层的细节。物理的薄片堆叠变成了架构。

senses.title: One coat of paint
senses.definition: one application or coat of paint, varnish or another covering material
senses.definitionCN: 油漆、清漆或其他覆盖材料的一次涂布
senses.example: The wall needs two more layers of paint.
senses.exampleCN: 这面墙还需要再刷两层漆。
senses.why: Painting is the most literal act of laying down a sheet of material. Each pass adds one more layer, and the old surface disappears under it.
senses.whyCN: 刷漆是最字面的“铺下一层材料”。每刷一遍就多一层，旧表面被盖在下面。

senses.title: Clothing stacked for warmth
senses.titleCN: 为保暖叠穿：一层层衣物
senses.definition: one garment or set of garments worn over another, especially for warmth
senses.definitionCN: 穿在另一件外面的一件或多件衣物，尤为了保暖
senses.example: Wear several thin layers instead of one thick coat.
senses.exampleCN: 穿几层薄衣服，而不是一件厚外套。
senses.why: Dressing in layers is stacking sheets of fabric around the body. Each garment is a layer, and warmth comes from the trapped air between them.
senses.whyCN: 分层穿衣就是把一片片布料叠在身体周围。每件衣服是一层，温暖来自层与层之间被困住的空气。

senses.title: The hen that lays
senses.definition: a hen kept for laying eggs, or a hen that lays eggs regularly
senses.definitionCN: 为产蛋而饲养的母鸡，或定期下蛋的母鸡
senses.example: The farm keeps two hundred layers.
senses.exampleCN: 这个农场养了两百只产蛋鸡。
senses.why: This is the agent sense of -er: a layer is 'one who lays'. It is not a sheet at all, but the same suffix that names the one performing the action.
senses.whyCN: 这是 -er 的施动者义：layer 就是“下蛋的那一个”。它完全不是薄片，而是同一个后缀用来命名执行动作的主体。

senses.title: Layering a plant
senses.titleCN: 压条繁殖：layer 的园艺动词
senses.definition: in gardening, to make a stem root while still attached to the parent plant, or the resulting rooted branch
senses.definitionCN: 园艺中使枝条在仍连着母株时生根，或指这样生根的枝条
senses.example: They layered the rose bush to produce a new plant.
senses.exampleCN: 他们对这株玫瑰进行压条，以培育新植株。
senses.why: The gardener bends a stem down and 'lays' it under soil. The new plant is produced by a laying-down, so the method and the verb share the original physical action.
senses.whyCN: 园丁把枝条弯下并“铺”在土里。新植株由一次“铺下”产生，所以这种方法与动词共享最初的物理动作。

intro.en: Layer is an English agent noun: lay + -er, 'one who or that which lays'. Lay goes back to Old English lecgan 'to place', from the causative of the verb that became lie. The 'sheet of material' sense developed later, probably under some influence from French cookery terms.
intro.cn: layer 是英语的施动名词：lay 加 -er，即“放置的人或物”。lay 可追溯到古英语 lecgan“放置”，它是后来变成 lie 的动词的使役形式。“一层材料”的义项发展较晚，可能受到法语烹饪用语的一些影响。

items.en: The root *legh- meant 'to lie down, lay'. It underlies English lie, lay and law (something 'laid down'), and German liegen and legen.
items.cn: 词根 *legh- 意为“躺下、放下”。它是英语 lie、lay 和 law（“被放下的东西”）以及德语 liegen、legen 的深层来源。

items.en: Lecgan meant 'to place on the ground or another surface; place in order; put down'. It was the causative of licgan 'to lie': to lay is to cause to lie.
items.cn: lecgan 意为“放在地上或其他表面上；按顺序摆放；放下”。它是 licgan“躺”的使役形式：lay 就是“使……躺下”。

items.en: Layer is first recorded in the late 14th century as 'one who or that lays', especially a mason who lays stones. This is the agent-noun sense of -er.
items.cn: layer 最早记录于 14 世纪晚期，意为“放置的人或物”，尤指砌石的泥瓦匠。这是 -er 的施动名词义。

items.en: The passive sense 'a thickness of material laid over a surface' is recorded by the 1610s. Because the earliest English uses were in cookery, the sense may have been influenced by French liue 'binding', a word used of a thickened sauce.
items.cn: 被动义“铺在表面上的一层材料”记录于 17 世纪 10 年代。由于英语最早的用法出现在烹饪中，这个义项可能受到法语 liue“黏合”的影响，后者用于浓稠酱汁。

items.en: The hen sense 'a hen that lays eggs' is recorded by 1707. Layer cake is attested from 1875, naming a cake made of stacked layers.
items.cn: “下蛋的母鸡”义项记录于 1707 年。layer cake（千层蛋糕）记录于 1875 年，指由叠层制成的蛋糕。

items.en: The verb layer is from 1779 in horticulture, as a method of plant propagation. The general sense 'form into layers' is attested by 1852.
items.cn: 动词 layer 来自 1779 年的园艺用法，指一种植物繁殖方法。“形成层”的一般义项记录于 1852 年。

note.en: The look-alike group is the lay/layer family; the near-meaning group contains words for sheets and levels, each from a different material or scale.
note.cn: 形近组是 lay/layer 词族；近义组是薄片与层级类词，各自的材料或尺度不同。

entries.definition: to put something down on a surface; to place in order. It is the verb behind layer, and its past tense is laid, not layed.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物放在表面上；按顺序摆放。它是 layer 背后的动词，过去式是 laid，不是 layed。

entries.definition: the act of putting something down, or of a hen producing an egg. It is the -ing form of lay.
entries.definitionCN: 放下某物的动作，或母鸡下蛋。它是 lay 的 -ing 形式。

entries.definition: arranged in layers, or having several levels. The past participle became an adjective describing a stacked structure.
entries.definitionCN: 分层排列的，或具有多个层次的。过去分词变成形容词，描述堆叠结构。

entries.definition: a layer of rock or soil, especially one of many deposited in sequence. It is the technical Latin word for a geological layer.
entries.definitionCN: 岩石或土壤的一层，尤指按顺序沉积的许多层之一。它是地质层的拉丁技术词。

entries.definition: a thin layer of a substance covering a surface. It stresses the material spread over something, often for protection.
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖在表面上的一薄层物质。它强调铺在表面的材料，常带保护目的。

entries.definition: a very thin layer or membrane. It is thinner than a typical layer and often continuous and transparent.
entries.definitionCN: 极薄的一层或膜。它比一般的 layer 更薄，常是连续而透明的。

entries.definition: one of several levels in a hierarchy, especially when they are ranked. It is the social or organizational counterpart of a physical layer.
entries.definitionCN: 等级体系中的一层，尤指被排序的层级。它是物理 layer 在社会或组织中的对应词。

normalIntro.en: Real pieces only: lay 'place down' + -er, plus the ordinary family layered, layering, multilayer, interlayer. The 'sheet' sense came later than the 'one who lays' sense.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实构件：lay“放下”加 -er，以及常用词族 layered、layering、multilayer、interlayer。“薄层”义晚于“放置者”义出现。

normal.en: Layer = lay + -er. The first meaning was 'one who lays', like a mason laying stones; only later did it mean 'that which is laid' as a sheet.
normal.cn: layer = lay + -er。最早的意思是“放置者”，像砌石的泥瓦匠；后来才表示“被铺下的东西”，即一层。

normal.en: A hen that lays eggs is also a layer, because -er can name the doer. The same suffix gives both the mason and the sheet.
normal.cn: 下蛋的母鸡也是 layer，因为 -er 可以命名动作的执行者。同一个后缀既给出泥瓦匠，也给出薄层。

normal.en: A geological layer is history stacked: each sheet of sediment is an older page under a newer one.
normal.cn: 地层就是被叠起来的历史：每一片沉积物都是压在更新一页下面的旧页。

normal.en: In computing, a layer hides the layer below it. The stack is physical in origin and architectural in use.
normal.cn: 在计算机中，一层隐藏下面一层。这个堆叠起源于物理，却被用于架构。

normal.en: Fixed patterns: a thin layer of, the ozone layer, layers of meaning, and in layers.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：a thin layer of（薄薄一层）、the ozone layer（臭氧层）、layers of meaning（层层含义）、in layers（分层地）。

abstract.en: A layer is both a cover and a record: it hides what is below while preserving it.
abstract.cn: 一层既是覆盖，也是记录：它遮住下面的东西，同时把它保存下来。

abstract.en: Complexity is often just depth: when a thing has too many layers, we stop seeing the surface and start seeing a system.
abstract.cn: 复杂往往只是深度：当一个东西层数太多，我们就不再看到表面，而开始看到一个系统。

abstract.en: Every layer was laid by someone or something. The word keeps the action inside the noun, which is why a stratum can be read as a date.
abstract.cn: 每一层都是由某个力量铺下的。这个词把动作保留在名词里，所以一层地层可以被读成一个年代。

examples.en: A thick layer of snow covered the car.
examples.cn: 厚厚的一层雪盖住了汽车。

examples.en: The problem has several layers that must be solved separately.
examples.cn: 这个问题有几层，必须分别解决。

examples.en: The farmer keeps a hundred layers for eggs.
examples.cn: 农场主养了一百只产蛋鸡。

dict_mnemonic.text: “累·尔”——累（了就把）尔（等薄片）一层层叠起来 → layer 层

root: 由英语动词 lay“放下、铺下”加施动后缀 -er 构成；lay 源于古英语 lecgan“放置”，再上溯到原始印欧语 *legh-“躺下、放下”，核心是“被铺下去的一片”，也保留“放置者”的施动义。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of layer, all one action: something is laid down on something else. Dust, meaning, rock, atmosphere, software, paint, clothing, a laying hen and a propagated stem each come from that same verb lay.
sensesIntro.cn: layer 的九个义项都是同一个动作：某物被铺在另一物上。灰尘、意义、岩石、大气、软件、油漆、衣物、下蛋的母鸡和压条的枝条，都来自同一个动词 lay。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: thin sheets stacked one on another, each visible as a separate band.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张张薄片叠在一起，每一片都能被看成分明的一带。

branches.en: MATERIAL LAID ON A SURFACE: dust, paint and clothing are added as sheets over what is already there.
branches.cn: 铺在表面上的材料：灰尘、油漆和衣物都是一片片加在已有之物上面。

branches.en: LEVELS IN A SYSTEM: meanings and software are built as stacks, each level resting on another.
branches.cn: 系统中的层级：意义与软件都以堆叠方式建立，每一层依托另一层。

branches.en: NATURAL BANDS: rock strata record ages, and atmospheric shells wrap the planet in bands.
branches.cn: 自然界的层带：岩层记录年代，大气壳层以带状包裹地球。

branches.en: THE DOER: a laying hen is a layer because -er can name the one performing the action.
branches.cn: 执行者：下蛋的母鸡是 layer，因为 -er 可以命名执行动作的主体。

branches.en: THE HORTICULTURAL ACT: a stem is laid under soil so that it roots, turning the verb back into a physical laying-down.
branches.cn: 园艺动作：枝条被铺在土下以便生根，使动词回到物理上的“铺下”。

intro.en: Layer is an English compound of lay + -er. Its family is built with -ed, -ing, and the prefixes multi- and inter-.
intro.cn: layer 是 lay + -er 的英语复合词。它的词族用 -ed、-ing，以及前缀 multi-、inter- 构成。

latinIntro.en: Layer has no Latin root; it is native English. The Latin word for a geological layer is stratum, from sternere 'to spread out', which is a useful contrast rather than a source.
latinIntro.cn: layer 没有拉丁词根，是本族英语词。地质层的拉丁词是 stratum，来自 sternere“铺开”，这是有用的对照，而不是来源。

items.meaning: a sheet laid over a surface; one who lays
items.meaningCN: 层；放置者（-er 表施动者或事物）
items.example: A layer of ice formed on the pond.

items.meaning: several sheets or levels; the act of layering
items.meaningCN: 多层；分层（复数或第三人称单数）

items.example: The story has a layered structure.

items.meaning: the act of arranging in layers; plant propagation
items.example: Layering is a simple way to propagate plants.
items.exampleCN: 压条是一种简单的植物繁殖方法。
这种薄膜使用多层包装。

items.meaningCN: 夹层；中间层（inter- 表之间）
items.example: A thin interlayer separates the two sheets.
items.exampleCN: 一层薄薄的夹层把两片材料隔开。

items.meaning: a cake made of stacked layers
items.example: She baked a chocolate layer cake.
items.exampleCN: 她烤了一个巧克力千层蛋糕。

items.meaning: the atmospheric band rich in ozone
items.example: The ozone layer absorbs ultraviolet light.

items.meaningCN: 放置；铺下（layer 的基础动词）
items.example: She laid the cloth on the table.

latinEntries.meaning: a layer, bed, pavement (not the source of layer)
latinEntries.meaningCN: 层；地层（并非 layer 的来源，仅作对照）

latinEntries.meaning: bed, couch (same PIE root as lay)
latinEntries.meaningCN: 床；卧榻（与 lay 同出一个原始印欧语词根）

definition_zh: 布局；版面设计；布置；规划图
definition_en: the way in which parts of something are arranged; the arrangement of text and pictures on a page; a plan showing such an arrangement
core_image: 桌面上摊开的图纸，方块、线条和标注被摆成清楚的位置关系
scene: 设计师把桌上的草图推开一点，重新摆放照片和标题的位置。The designer changed the layout of the page to give the photos more room.
sceneCN: 这里是「版面布局」（第 1 个义项：各部分在页面上的安排）；句意是设计师调整了页面布局，给照片留出更多空间。图中可辨识物件：草图、照片、标题。

pos.zh: 布局；版面设计；布置；规划图

derivatives.zh: 由 lay 与 out 组成的短语动词，义为「布置；摊开；排版」
由 re- 与 layout 复合而成，义为「重新布局」
由 lay out 的过去分词形式构成，义为「布置好的；摊开的」

senses.title: The arrangement of text and pictures on a page
senses.definition: the way text, pictures and empty space are arranged on a page or screen
senses.definitionCN: 文字、图片与空白在页面或屏幕上的安排方式
senses.example: The designer changed the layout of the page to give the photos more room.
senses.exampleCN: 设计师调整了页面布局，给照片留出更多空间。
senses.why: Lay out first meant to spread things on a surface; printers then used it for placing type and images, and the noun kept that page sense.
senses.whyCN: lay out 最初指把东西摊在平面上；印刷者随后用它指摆放字与图，名词便保留了这层页面义。

senses.title: The way parts of a place are arranged
senses.definition: the arrangement of furniture, rooms or objects within a space
senses.definitionCN: 家具、房间或物件在某一空间内的安排
senses.example: The new layout of the kitchen puts the sink under the window.
senses.exampleCN: 厨房的新布局把水槽放到了窗下。
senses.why: A room is laid out much like a page: things are placed in relation to one another, and the same noun serves both.
senses.whyCN: 房间的布置很像页面的排版：物件按彼此关系摆放，同一个名词便兼指两者。

senses.title: A plan or diagram of an arrangement
senses.definition: a drawing or plan that shows how something is or will be arranged
senses.definitionCN: 表明某物现状或未来安排方式的图样或规划
senses.example: The engineer handed us a layout of the factory floor.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师递给我们一张车间平面布置图。
senses.why: Once an arrangement is fixed, it can be drawn; the drawing takes the same name because it records the very placement the word describes.
senses.whyCN: 安排一旦确定就能画成图；图纸沿用同一个名字，因为它记录的正是这个词所描述的摆放方式。

intro.en: Layout is a nineteenth-century English compound: the verb lay out, meaning to spread or arrange, became a noun for the arrangement itself.
intro.cn: layout 是十九世纪的英语复合词：短语动词 lay out（摊开、布置）变成了指安排本身的名词。

items.en: Lay comes from the Old English verb lecgan, to put something down.
items.cn: lay 来自古英语动词 lecgan，意为把东西放下。

items.en: Middle English used lay out for spreading things on a surface.
items.cn: 中古英语用 lay out 表示把东西摊开在平面上。

items.en: The phrasal verb lay out came to mean arranging a room, a page or a plan.
items.cn: 短语动词 lay out 逐渐表示布置房间、排版或规划。

items.en: In the nineteenth century the two words were joined into the noun layout.
items.cn: 十九世纪，这两个词合并成名词 layout。

items.en: Modern English uses layout for pages, rooms, factories and computer screens.
items.cn: 现代英语用 layout 指页面、房间、工厂和电脑屏幕的布局。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms of the phrasal verb and one compound with another meaning; the near-meaning group collects words for arrangement and design.
note.cn: 形近组收短语动词的各种形式和一个意义不同的复合词；近义组收表示安排与设计的词。

entries.definition: To spread something out or to arrange it according to a plan.
entries.definitionCN: 把东西摊开，或按计划加以布置。

entries.definition: Arranged or spread out in a particular way.
entries.definitionCN: 按某种方式布置好或摊开的。

entries.definition: An amount of money spent on something; the parts look alike but the meaning is different.
entries.definitionCN: 为某事花出的一笔钱；两个成分拼写相同，但词义不同。

entries.definition: A new or repeated arrangement of a page or space.
entries.definitionCN: 对页面或空间重新进行的布局。

entries.definition: The way things are put in order or in position.
entries.definitionCN: 事物被排成顺序或摆好位置的方式。

entries.definition: A plan or pattern made before something is built.
entries.definitionCN: 在建造之前拟定的计划或样式。

entries.definition: The arrangement of parts to form a whole, especially in art.
entries.definitionCN: 各部分组成整体的安排，尤用于艺术。

entries.definition: The shape, size and general arrangement of a page or file.
entries.definitionCN: 页面或文件的形状、尺寸与总体安排。

normalIntro.en: The word is a compound of a Germanic verb and a particle, and its senses all keep the idea of placing things into a plan.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由一个日耳曼语动词和一个副词小品词复合而成，各义项都保留「把东西放进计划」的想法。

normal.en: Lay out began as a verb meaning to spread things on a surface, and layout simply froze that action into a noun.
normal.cn: lay out 起初是动词，意为把东西摊在平面上，layout 则把这个动作凝固成名词。

normal.en: Page layout is the oldest noun sense: printers laid out type before they printed a sheet.
normal.cn: page layout 是最早的名词义：印刷者在印一张纸之前先摆放活字。

normal.en: Office layout and kitchen layout use the same idea on furniture and rooms instead of type and pictures.
normal.cn: office layout 和 kitchen layout 把同一想法用到家具和房间上，而不是字与图。

normal.en: A layout plan is the drawing of the arrangement, which is why the noun can also name a diagram.
normal.cn: layout plan 是布局的图纸，所以这个名词也能指一张图。

normal.en: Relayout adds re- to layout, so it means arranging the same space or page again.
normal.cn: relayout 在 layout 前加 re-，意为把同一空间或页面重新布置。

abstract.en: Layout is what turns a pile of things into a readable space, whether paper, room or factory.
abstract.cn: layout 把一堆东西变成可读的空间，无论是纸张、房间还是工厂。

abstract.en: The same word covers the act, the result and the drawing of an arrangement, because planning leaves all three behind.
abstract.cn: 同一个词覆盖动作、结果和图纸，因为规划会留下这三样东西。

abstract.en: A good layout is invisible: we notice it only when the parts refuse to fit.
abstract.cn: 好的布局是看不见的：只有当各部分配不上时，我们才会注意它。

examples.en: The designer changed the layout of the page to give the photos more room.
examples.cn: 设计师调整了页面布局，给照片留出更多空间。

examples.en: The new layout of the kitchen puts the sink under the window.
examples.cn: 厨房的新布局把水槽放到了窗下。

examples.en: The engineer handed us a layout of the factory floor.
examples.cn: 工程师递给我们一张车间平面布置图。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「累奥特」——设计师排完版面累得直说奥特；layout 是布局。

root: 由英语动词 lay（古英语 lecgan，放下）与副词 out 复合，十九世纪固化为名词 layout。

sensesIntro.en: The core is arrangement; the senses divide into page design, the arrangement of a space, and the drawing that records it.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是安排；义项由此分为页面设计、空间布置，以及记录安排方式的图纸。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: sheets of paper on a desk, with blocks and lines placed into clear positions.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌面上摊开的纸张，方块与线条被摆成清楚的位置关系。

branches.en: a page where photos and text find their places
branches.cn: 照片与文字各就其位的页面

branches.en: a print proof marked with arrows and boxes
branches.cn: 用箭头和方框标出的校样

branches.en: a room rearranged around one window
branches.cn: 围绕一扇窗重新布置的房间

branches.en: a factory plan spread on a table
branches.cn: 摊在桌上的工厂平面图

branches.en: a screen divided into panels and menus
branches.cn: 被分成面板与菜单的屏幕

intro.en: A Germanic verb plus an English particle form the compound, and re- plus a participle show how the word keeps growing.
intro.cn: 一个日耳曼语动词加一个英语小品词构成这个复合词，而 re- 与过去分词又显示它仍在生长。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.meaningCN: 构成短语名词的小品词

definition_zh: 领导；带领；导致；领先
definition_en: to guide or be in charge of others, to cause something to happen, or to be ahead
core_image: 一个人走在队伍最前面，身后的人跟着他选的方向
scene: 队伍在岔路口停下，向导抬手示意大家往左边走。She led the group through the narrow pass.
sceneCN: 这里是「带领、引导」（第 1 个义项：动词，指走在前头带路）；句意为她带着队伍穿过狭窄的山口。图中可辨识物件：岔路口、向导的手势、狭窄山口。

derivatives.zh: 由 lead 加 -er 构成，义为「领导者；领袖」
由 lead 加 -ing 构成，义为「领先的；主要的」
由 leader 加 -ship 构成，义为「领导；领导力」
由 mis-（错误地）加 lead 构成，义为「误导」

senses.title: To guide someone along a way
senses.definition: to go in front of others and show them the way
senses.definitionCN: 走在别人前面并为他们指路
senses.example: She led the group through the narrow pass.
senses.exampleCN: 她带着队伍穿过狭窄的山口。
senses.why: The Old English verb meant to cause someone to go; the leader is the one who sets the direction of that going.
senses.whyCN: 这个古英语动词本义是「使某人走」，带路的人就是决定「往哪走」的那个人。

senses.title: To be in charge of people or an activity
senses.definition: to direct a group, organization or activity and be responsible for it
senses.definitionCN: 指挥一个群体、组织或活动并对其负责
senses.example: He leads a team of twelve engineers.
senses.exampleCN: 他领导着一支十二名工程师的团队。
senses.why: From physically going first it is a short step to deciding for others, so lead comes to mean holding authority.
senses.whyCN: 从身体上走在最前，很容易走到「替别人做决定」，于是 lead 转而指掌握权力。

senses.title: To cause something to happen
senses.definition: to be the cause or route by which a result happens
senses.definitionCN: 成为某个结果发生的原因或路径
senses.example: Poor sleep can lead to serious health problems.
senses.exampleCN: 睡眠不足可能导致严重的健康问题。
senses.why: A path leads to a place; events also have paths, so lead to names the route by which one thing brings about another.
senses.whyCN: 一条路通向一个地方；事情也有路径，所以 lead to 指一件事带出另一件事的路线。

senses.title: To be ahead in a race or competition
senses.definition: to have more points or be further forward than others in a contest
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛中比别人得分多或位置更靠前
senses.example: Our team leads by two goals.
senses.exampleCN: 我们队领先两球。
senses.why: The one in front is literally leading the line, and the racing sense keeps that simple picture of position.
senses.whyCN: 走在最前的人字面上就在「带」着队伍，竞赛义保留了这个简单的方位画面。

senses.title: The position of being ahead
senses.definition: the first place or advantage held over others in a contest
senses.definitionCN: 在竞争中占据的第一名次或优势
senses.example: The champion held the lead until the final lap.
senses.exampleCN: 冠军一直保持领先直到最后一圈。
senses.why: The verb's sense of being in front turns into a noun naming that front position.
senses.whyCN: 动词「处在前面」的意思转成一个名词，指那个靠前的位置。

senses.title: A clue in an investigation
senses.definition: a piece of information that suggests where to look next
senses.definitionCN: 提示下一步该往哪里查的信息
senses.example: The police followed a new lead.
senses.exampleCN: 警方追查了一条新线索。
senses.why: A lead is something that leads you somewhere; in an investigation it is the information that pulls the search forward.
senses.whyCN: lead 是能把你带到某处的东西；在调查里，它就是推动搜查往前走的信息。

intro.en: Lead comes from an Old English verb meaning to cause to go, and it has kept the picture of someone walking in front.
intro.cn: lead 来自古英语中意为「使……走」的动词，一直保留着「有人走在前面」的画面。

items.en: Lædan meant to cause someone to go, to guide or to bring along a way.
items.cn: lædan 意为使某人走、引导或沿路带领。

items.en: The reconstructed verb *laidijan is related to the noun for a path or way.
items.cn: 重构动词 *laidijan 与表示「道路、路径」的名词有关。

items.en: Middle English leden keeps the sense of guiding and adds the idea of being first in a group.
items.cn: 中古英语 leden 保留引导义，并添上「在群体中最先」的意思。

items.en: The noun lead, meaning the first place, appears in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 表示第一名的名词 lead 在十五世纪出现。

items.en: Modern English adds lead to 'cause' and lead as a clue, while the metal lead is a different word with a different vowel.
items.cn: 现代英语添上 lead to（导致）与「线索」义；金属铅则是另一个词，元音也不同。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers inflections and relatives of the verb; the near-meaning group gathers words for guiding and being first.
note.cn: 形近组收动词的变形与同族词；近义组收表示引导与领先的词。

entries.definition: The past tense and past participle of lead.
entries.definitionCN: lead 的过去式与过去分词。

entries.definition: A person who leads a group.
entries.definitionCN: 领导者；领袖。

entries.definition: Most important or in first place.
entries.definitionCN: 领先的；主要的。

entries.definition: To guide someone in the wrong direction.
entries.definitionCN: 误导；把某人带错方向。

entries.definition: To show someone the way.
entries.definitionCN: 引导；带路。

entries.definition: To organize and carry out an activity.
entries.definitionCN: 组织；进行。

entries.definition: To control or manage an activity.
entries.definitionCN: 指挥；管理。

entries.definition: To be the leader of a group.
entries.definitionCN: 领导；作为……的首领。

normalIntro.en: The past tense led drops the a of the present, and the family shows how guiding, leading and causing are one motion.
normalIntro.cn: 过去式 led 去掉了现在式中的 a；词族显示引导、领导与导致是同一种运动。

normal.en: The past tense is led, not leaded: lead, led, led.
normal.cn: 过去式是 led，不是 leaded：lead、led、led。

normal.en: Leader adds -er: the one who leads.
normal.cn: leader 加 -er，指带路的人。

normal.en: Lead to means to cause a result, as a road leads to a town.
normal.cn: lead to 意为导致结果，就像路通向城镇。
